chosen_option_text: “We cannot possibly let this go ahead!” spits your eternally-angry Chief of Enforcement Ashley Bourdain, clutching her fists tighter by the second. “Blocking those gorgeous views of Vanilla Llama City is bad enough, but boasting such obnoxious disrespect for our glorious government is nothing short of treason! Any building, or billionaire for that matter, to purposefully inconvenience you ought to be judged more damningly than to simply call them ‘spiteful’. Give my team the nod and I’ll have any eyesore you want demolished or hubristic billionaire arrested before sundown.”

title: Let Them Eat Rainbow Cake!
text: When high-profile lesbian celebrity Ellen Lynch was asked to leave popular establishment The Vanilla Llama City Diner, it was made clear to her that this was because she was dining with her lesbian partner. The restaurant owners refused to serve the homosexual couple, citing a conflict with their religious beliefs. This isn’t the first time something like this has been flagged by the press, but Lynch is keen to make some noise.
chosen_option_text: The Deputy Mayor of Vanilla Llama City, Cillian Shaft strides in, dashingly pink trench coat flapping in the breeze behind him. “The mayor won’t like this, but if we want Vanilla Llama to be a prestigious and progressive nation on the world stage, we’ve got to go even further! To cater for... that is to protect the rights of the gay community, we should establish zones in each restaurant or other service industry venture that are reserved exclusively for gay and lesbian people. Think of our standing in the international gay community! Think of the tourism! We’d be a shining beacon for gay culture!”

title: Much Ado About Abortion
text: A monstrous debate between pro-life and pro-choice groups has erupted after a high-profile case of a pregnant woman aborting her foetus because she ‘didn’t feel like it’ hit the tabloids.
chosen_option_text: “Abortion has to be legal if we’re going to last as a nation,” says Brynlee Windass, President of the Society of Bitter Old People. “Have you ever thought that with our nation’s growing population of 56 million, we soon aren’t going to be able to squeeze any more people into Vanilla Llama? If we use abortion to control the population, we’ll make great savings and can spend the money elsewhere. One child per family should just about do it I think. Extraneous ones can be sold to other countries.”

title: Dangerous Liaisons
text: Your brother just broke up with his most recent girlfriend. However, this one turned out to be a bit different from all his previous love interests.
chosen_option_text: “Although I agree with your brother’s diagnoses, I disagree with his method of rehabilitation,” states Milo Guterres, a psychiatrist, as he beckons your brother to a leather couch. “Serial stalkers are known to have mental disorders that increase their infatuation with the object of their desire, leading to irrational and anti-social behaviour. Prison time will not cure them. What they need is an extensive course of cognitive behavioural therapy, where they will learn to decode, process, and alter their warped thinking patterns.”

title: Compulsory Gun Ownership?
text: This weekend, a citizen’s group calling itself Gun Owners of Vanilla Llama has petitioned Congress with a controversial bill making gun ownership compulsory.
chosen_option_text: “While the Gun Owners of Vanilla Llama have the safety and security of our people in mind, it would simply be impractical to enforce,” comments Police Chief Kellyanne Harrison. “A better option would be to legalize, and encourage use of, concealed carry laws, which would allow responsible citizens to keep firearms with them at all times, on their person, to kill any wacko or their cousin who they think is threatening them.”

title: Some People Never Listen
text: Two senior officials caught having affairs, five separate expenses scandals and the leaking of top-secret plans for the Cabinet Secretary’s birthday party is usually more than enough to cover in one public announcement. You were therefore surprised to find that another issue altogether has caught the public’s attention: activists representing the nation’s deaf and hearing-impaired communities have taken you to task over the lack of a Vanilla Llaman Sign Language interpreter at your public addresses.
chosen_option_text: “Being deaf doesn’t have to be an impairment, so don’t make it one,” signs activist Bongani Coleman, adding a few more vulgar hand gestures that you are sure aren’t official sign language. “Having an interpreter is the least you could do. Deaf people in Vanilla Llama are subject to a harmful mix of preconceptions and ignorance, so it’s about time you listened to us. Perhaps you could also establish a national ‘Deaf Awareness Week’ to celebrate the contributions deaf people have made to society, and to persuade organisations and individuals to bear us in mind.”

title: Gone Girls
text: All of Vanilla Llama has been desperate for news of Amelie Adams, a Vanilla Llaman teenager who went missing yesterday. Search parties have been gathered, rivers are being dredged, and thermal-camera-wielding helicopters are scouring every inch of the nation. As you receive another hourly update on ‘Amazing Amelie’, a Bigtopian mother approaches you with a tear-soaked picture.
chosen_option_text: “Look, I’m no racist,” booms Nomfundo Bowie, Grand Supreme High Dude of local ‘group of friends’ Blanking Big-Nosed Bigtopians, adjusting her conspicuously pointed white hood. “But we all know those types: criminals! Don’t let them abuse government resources just because they can’t control their kids. Everyone knows they all wind up as hardened thugs — jaywalking, listening to aggressive Bigtopian music, selling authentic Northern Vanilla Llaman headgear without a permit... Scum! These bigwig kids are just out of control. Mark them all down as the runaways they are and get back to the real victims: the innocent Vanilla Llaman doves like Amazing Amelie.”

title: Animation Provocation
text: When media boss Ian Tivruski green-lighted a new Brancalandian animated series for the Vanilla Llaman Kids Network, he thought he was commissioning a delightful children’s show about metal-working amazons who knit cozy jumpers for their grandkids. As it turns out, the surprisingly explicit animation Sword Heroins: Love Needle has caused a lot of confusion amongst young viewers, and upset many parents.
chosen_option_text: “I think we’re ignoring a broader issue here,” bemoans frustrated animator Parker Stonetrey, “which is that animated art forms are never taken seriously enough to be considered anything more than kiddie fare. I say that we develop Vanilla Llama’s artistic vision and creativity by subsidising adult animation. When people think Vanilla Llama, they should think hentai!”

title: All That Glitters
text: When a celebrity power couple like pro-footballer Bruno Green and fashion model and former pop starlet Prudence Mulder marries, there’s bound to be some glitz and glamour. In fact, thanks to Prudence’s obsession with being a “fairytale princess” the beachside wedding also involved many tonnes of glitter, which is now drifting across the nearby lagoon, raising an important question — what about the mess?
chosen_option_text: “Awww but the glitter is LUVVERLY,” coos the blushing bride, her ultra-thin arms flapping as they catch a weak breeze. “We should make all the beaches and streets look all pretty and glittery, innit? It’d be so nice, and everyone would be smiling all the time because... because... AWWW I LOVE GLITTER, ME!”

title: Short Shorts Too Short?
text: Dress codes for young women are in the news again after a violent clash between parents on opposite sides of the issue. The ringleaders have been dragged into your office by your Minister of Education for an impromptu arbitration and time-out.
chosen_option_text: Finally, fifteen year old Samus sits down at your desk, barely looking at you while she types vigorously at her smartphone. “Jeez, like, get off my back. I can, like, wear whatever I want. Boys are so stupid sometimes. Look at these shorts; they’re even patriotic!” She stands up and does a twirl to show her short shorts are in your national colours with Vanilla Llama emblazoned across the backside. “Pretty nice right?” She smacks her gum loudly, takes a selfie, and goes back to texting.

title: A Timely Intervention
text: You and your cabinet are on a tour of the nearby Vanilla Llama Watch Factory, which has long been famous throughout all of Land of Faceplace. The poor state of the factory — and its rapidly declining sales figures, carelessly left on the manager’s desk — are clear for all to see. Shuffling by your side, the manager sighs: “Leader, we’ve had some tough years here. But we don’t know what to do to bring the good days back.”
chosen_option_text: “The hour is at hand! This is the time of Violet!” shouts Violetist priest Paul Thawne through an open window. “The time spent watching these evil little machinations would be better spent praising the almighty Violet! We must rid ourselves of this factory of evil, seeking and burning all its offspring; wherever it may hide in our land! Violet demands that the government ban and destroy every horological horror, for — as is written in the texts — there is no reason or rhyme, no meaning or time but by Violet’s dread love!” The priest tries to light a match but is dragged away by your bodyguards.

title: O Fortuna!
text: JACKPOT! It seemed impossible, it seemed unlikely, it seemed as if the odds would not favour you. Yet you, Leader, are the lucky winner of a major cash prize from last night’s national lottery, thanks to that lottery ticket your mother had gifted you for Maxxmas. Yet before you can even celebrate, you realize that your good fortune has made national headlines.
chosen_option_text: “Did mommy dear put your name on the lottery ticket? No? Good!” exclaims your brother while unceremoniously snatching the fortuitous piece of paper from your hand. “Just say that the ticket was mine, and all you’ll have to deal with is a few angry stares for a while. You’ve dealt with worse! This way, our family will be happy, all thanks to the numbers 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, and 42. But don’t worry, if you ever lose your office, your dear, old brother will take care of you...”

title: Pure Madness
text: Purity balls have become the latest craze among some social conservatives in Vanilla Llama, with many sexual abstinence groups endorsing a ceremony where teenage girls promise to remain chaste until they get married, wearing a ring as a token of that promise. Feminist groups, however, have denounced this practice.
chosen_option_text: “This is patriarchy at its worst!” yells women’s rights advocate Samde Duras, author of critical thesis Purity: A History of Ball-Holding in Vanilla Llama. “I can’t bear to see any more photos of adolescent girls wearing wedding gowns, pledging their chastity to fathers dressed as bridegrooms. These men seem to think they own their daughters’ bodies, to be transferred to their sons-in-law! Look, Leader, I don’t care if a woman wants to remain a virgin until she gets married, but these purity balls objectify women and should be banned.”

title: Market Crash
text: On a busy Saturday morning, a minicab driver took a shortcut through a crowded market street. After skidding on some banana peels, he lost control and crashed through a dozen fruit and vegetable stalls, narrowly avoiding injuring anyone. Pedestrians are donning full body armor, and Vanilla Llamen are beginning to accept that reckless driving and speeding in the inner city may be just another fact of life.
chosen_option_text: “Why don’t you just pedestrianise a big chunk of the city centre?” suggests tourist Simon Turner, adjusting his anti-smog facemask. “It’ll make the whole area much prettier, quieter and cleaner, and it’ll let you show off the beauty of the heart of the city.”

title: This Green and Pleasant Land
text: Good news, everyone! An unexpected rise in the water table has transformed a million acres of former desert into green and fertile and farming-ready land. As the government owns this land, it’s now up to you what you do with it.
chosen_option_text: “Excuse me, is anyone going to ask why this has happened?” asks party-pooping scientist Ming Holt. “We can’t make use of this land till we understand what happened. I suggest establishing a research station here, and getting a better understanding of the ecological changes that led to this fertile land emerging.”

title: Is There an Election in Marche Noire or Are You Just Happy to See Us?
text: Facing a tight political race at home, Otto Kratt, the authoritarian leader of Marche Noire, and his cronies plan to clinch his fourth reelection by campaigning for the votes of Marche Noirian emigrants in Vanilla Llama. Alarmed and angered by his many flagrant violations of human rights, socially-conscious protestors have demanded that you forbid him from propagating his vitriolic views on Vanilla Llaman soil in order to hamper his chances of victory.
chosen_option_text: “Putrid lies!” howls Sierra Prefect, a supportive Marche Noirian immigrant carrying a life-size cardboard cutout of Otto Kratt. “We love Otto Kratt! He is the most wonderful and glorious leader of Marche Noire who cares deeply for us when he chooses. He has every right to talk to his kinsmen wherever they are! You keep saying that people here have freedom of speech, yet you would deprive our ruler of his freedom to speak to us now? Leader, you must allow Mr. Kratt to campaign and organize rallies here.”

title: Imitation Station
text: While chauffeuring you to work this morning, your driver notified you of a recent spike in motorized vehicle accidents. He says that the cause is several distracting radio advertisements - one ironically telling drivers to “buckle up”. These ads include sounds of screams, screeching tyres, honking horns, and police sirens, causing confusion for drivers on the road.
chosen_option_text: “Whoa, whoa, whoa, let’s slow down here, people,” says grumpy middle-aged woman Vera Kimmel. “There is an incredibly easy solution here, and that’s just to not allow radios or any other audio systems in cars. Think about it! No more young drivers ‘sharing’ the latest chart tunes at full volume as they drive through town centres, no more screaming toddlers demanding that nursery rhymes are on endless loop on long car journeys and no more sad songs making you want to take a hard left into oblivion when you’re driving along the clifftop. Wait, is that one just me?”

title: Subpar Suburbs
text: A water main burst in a suburb of Vanilla Llama City. After months of inaction, the pool of standing water has turned the now largely abandoned commercial district into a watering hole for local wildlife. Local businesses have come to you demanding change.
chosen_option_text: “Every one of these plans conveniently forgets about the animals,” chastises the head barista from Bean Me Up Coffee. “Y’all saunter in here after mother nature has made the best of a bad situation. That watering hole is crucial to the local wildlife, and it simply isn’t fair to take that away from the bunnies and deer and the cute little birds. Let’s take whatever money we were going to waste on rebuilding this failing town and turn it into a nature reserve.”

title: Skin’s the Wrong Colour
text: One of your nephews decided to go under the needle, and cover half of his body in a veritable panoply of tattoos depicting various scenes from a number of Nicolas Cage movies. As a result, he was fired from his job as a school receptionist.
chosen_option_text: Your nephew, flexing his arm to make Ghost Rider and H. I. McDunnough dance with each other, complains to you: “This is nothing less than obvious discrimination! I was excelling at my job, had Employee of the Month three times running, my colleagues said I was a kick-ass national treasure. But as soon as I got all inked up, my job was stolen from me, gone in sixty seconds, given away to my assistant Mandy. There goes my job at Ridgemont High! You have to stop businesses from discriminating against those who want to express themselves. In fact, you have to protect the rights of free expression and bodily autonomy, and make sure that nobody ever is discriminated against for what they choose to write or draw on their body. You know, it could happen to anyone, it could happen to you.”

title: Marriage by Proxy Server
text: After an online petition that would allow people to legally be married over the internet reached over one million signatures last night, you awake to find your inbox inundated with emails and a crowd of petitioners waiting inside your office, all demanding you take action.
chosen_option_text: “Oh, that’s a terrible idea!” chides your nettling aunt. “You have to be careful on the internet. You never know if the people you’re talking to really are who they say they are. Why just the other day, I was being courted by this youthful hunk of a gentleman on MatchMakers. But, when we finally met in person, the scoundrel was as old and flabby as me! It just goes to show that some things like dating and marriage should only be done offline and in person.”

title: The Lowest Form of Wit
text: Kamehameha Watson, your Minister of Health, became a target of criticism when he responded to a political opponent’s colorful insults by saying “Maybe you should consider rinsing your dirty mouth with bleach. It might even help you get rid of that bad breath.” Unfortunately, some citizens took this as actual advice that this would work as a treatment for their own stinky exhalations, and have been hospitalized with painful injuries.
chosen_option_text: “Look, it is not my problem that some people in this country aren’t the sharpest knives in the drawer,” sneers Watson, throwing his arms up in exasperation. “Sarcasm, people! It shouldn’t be so hard to understand. Even my 5-year-old niece got the joke. I guess the proles must be so adept at comprehending rhetorical devices because of our robustly funded education system, and you DON’T need to spend more on that. That was me being sarcastic again, in case you missed it. Yeesh.”

title: Cheerleading Community Does the Splits
text: When East Vanilla Llama City High School denied a male student’s request to join their cheerleading squad, they thought that was the end of it. Since then, the story has been picked up by the national media, with the boy, the cheerleading coach, and a spokesperson from Equality Vanilla Llama giving interviews about the controversy. Now, a gaggle of highly-opinionated and very-spirited individuals have entered your office, demanding your attention.
chosen_option_text: “Give me an ‘E’! Give me a ‘Q’! Give me a ‘U’-‘A’-‘L’! Give me an ‘I’, and a ‘T’, and a great big ‘Y’! What’s it spell? EQUALITY!” cries Dawa Barker, doing an impressive backflip routine in his plaid skirt. “Every boy deserves an equal chance to live out their dreams, whether that dream is to cheer a mediocre football team, or be on a mediocre football team! You must force every school to allow any individual to join any team they want, regardless of sex! Why not? Girls are just as strong as boys, and we boys can be darn cute in these skirts!” Cheering your name, he cartwheels out the door.

title: Going Off the Rails
text: With suicide-by-train incidents in Vanilla Llama’s stations becoming disturbingly common, commuters and rail operators are irritated by the impact on their day-to-day activities.
chosen_option_text: “People who try to kill themselves shouldn’t be punished for being ill, and neither should the families of victims of suicide,” your Minister of Health, Gene Tolkien, entreats passionately. “Being suicidal is often a sign of mental illness or depression, and our government mustn’t stoop to punishing families for having sick relatives. We ought to focus on suicide prevention rather than hounding these families for money, and we would save a lot of lives through education and extending a helping hand to those who need our support.”

title: Have Your Cake and Don’t Eat It
text: Sydney Pugwash, a young dancer, recently collapsed with the complications of what was revealed to be anorexia nervosa while dancing in the small, televised role of ‘Girl Waiting for Pater Maxxmas’. National attention has now been drawn to the growing prevalence of eating disorders and related hospitalizations in Vanilla Llama, especially among the dance community.
chosen_option_text: “Here’s some food for thought,” says psychologist Des Carter, handing you a copy of his new book Cogeato Ergo Sum: I Eat, Therefore I Am. “Eating disorders are growing year on year, in both male and female Vanilla Llamen. They may be the result of low self-esteem, body dysmorphia, or can be comorbid with other psychological disorders. Due to the high morbidity, it is vital that you subsidize psychiatric in-patient treatment and prevent future eating disorders by encouraging citizens to attend government funded therapy. Now, why don’t you lie down on this couch and tell me how you feel...”

title: A Right Not to Work?
text: High ranking officials and devout followers of a major religion have requested that the government close down retail stores during their weekly holy day, in accordance with their religious views.
chosen_option_text: Slacker freelance food reviewer Adele McDuck, still in pajamas and eating a pizza slice on a ratty couch, sends you a video chat invitation. “Dude, why not just give everybody shorter work weeks? Make flex time, telecommuting, and 35-hour work weeks mandatory for all us working folk. Trust me, the people will love you for it man!”

title: A Game Theory
text: A new study performed in East Vanilla Llama City High School showed a major increase in student engagement when video games were added to lessons. A gaggle of laptop-wielding citizens stand in your office, debating the role of video games in education.
chosen_option_text: The nephew you’re babysitting looks up from his tablet and babbles, “Know what I think? We should be playing games we actually like in school. BloxCraft taught me how to build things and be creative, and Furlough taught me friendship and teamwork! Give us some class time where we can play whatever video games we want. The teacher can even play too! That way we learn stuff and have fun! Oh, and I promise I won’t say naughty words when I die this time!”

title: The Deportation of Mr. B. Leeper
text: Brancalandian pop star Bryan Leeper has gotten into trouble with the law yet again while on tour in Vanilla Llama. He was caught urinating on a fire hydrant, making this his tenth arrest in the past year. Tens of thousands of anti-Bleepers have signed a petition demanding that the pop star be deported back to his native Brancaland.
chosen_option_text: “We don’t want the little brat back!” declares the Brancalandian Foreign Minister, seen smashing Bryan Leeper CDs with a hockey stick. “I bumped into the Maxtopian ambassador on my way here. It seems that Mr. Leeper has an outstanding legal issue over in Maxtopia that could involve jail time if he’s found guilty. Why not extradite him there as a diplomatic move? What’s that? Well yes, Maxtopia has the death penalty. I’m sure he hasn’t done anything that serious there.”

title: The Artwork in the Attic
text: After the death of the wealthy Maxtopian immigrant Emmeline Judi Webster,  a large stash of paintings, many of which are believed to have been produced by the most notable artists in the history of Maxtopia, was found in her attic.  With no will to reference, it is up to the government to decide what should be done with the discoveries.
chosen_option_text: “Pay to see them!” gasps Grogu Laine, the Maxtopian Minister of Culture and part-time art critic. “There are paintings of great historical and cultural value to my country in that collection!  They should be returned to Maxtopia with all due haste!  Just imagine ‘The Fall of St. Barrysburg’ hanging on the walls of the Maxtopian town house of Wilhelm Ruff, as the noises of war reached his ears from outside his study.  Does it not stir your soul?”

title: Wiggle Room
text: A curious new weight loss fad has wormed its way into the world of fat slimming in Vanilla Llama — deliberate self-infection with tapeworms.
chosen_option_text: “Let’s not open this can of worms too hastily,” cautions Cortana Kettering, a nerdy researcher from prominent pharmaceutical company Mhizer, as she flips through a thick clipboard containing colourful charts and coffee stains. “There’s been plenty of research into the risks and rewards of using tapeworms to lose weight, and there’s a pretty clear conclusion — it sucks, and we’re not referring to lost body weight. But, guess what? Thanks to rigorous trials conducted by yours truly, Mhizer’s approved weight loss pills can help you burn up to 10% of your body fat in a year without too much risk! It’s true, many consumers can’t afford conventional methods of losing weight, so you should subsidise the production of our wonder pills to give everyone the equal opportunity they deserve.”

title: Democracy Going to the Dogs?
text: After a recent election installed a small dog as a member of parliament, the fringe group “Brains for Ballots” has demanded for the government to tighten voting restrictions.
chosen_option_text: “Umm... huh?” inquires village idiot Peter Wildish. “I voted? When? Oh, yeah. Please don’t make me not vote. The ballots are really tasty, and where else would I get my fibre? Everyone should have the right to vote, no matter what their favourite greenhouse is! Then we can all get the government to do what we want! First thing I think we should do is, uh, ban fruit? I hate fruit.”

title: Mal Appetit!
text: Hugh Jass, Vanilla Llama’s most famous TV foodie, drew a lot of criticism when he visited a world-class restaurant in yesterday’s episode and gorged on expensive gourmet foods in a manner that some viewers found too “appetite-stimulating.” Mr. Jass’ extravagance was said to be particularly disrespectful to millions of poor Vanilla Llaman citizens who could not afford one of the dishes he ate with their entire monthly salary.
chosen_option_text: “Mon dieu!” grumbles Mr. Jass, sniffing his croissant, and throwing it away untouched. “Do these wretched ignorami not recognise the worth of a good tagliolini con tartufo? ‘Pasta with mushrooms’ indeed! If these peasants have neither the means nor aspiration to appreciate vicarious high-quality culinary culture, they can simply change the channel. I render a valuable service to our economy by giving publicity to our first-class restaurants. So, how about the government picks up the restaurant bills for our gastronomic journalism? I’ll cover the service charge, of course.”

title: Burn! Burn Everything!
text: A recent anti-government rally by highly disgruntled teens has brought a previously minor issue to the fore: should people be permitted to burn Vanilla Llama’s flag, or should it be a crime?
chosen_option_text: “These barbarians are suggesting burning the flag of our glorious nation as if it were a piece of scrap cloth! First it’s burning the flag, and before you know it, it’s rebellion and anarchy!” Kathryn Edwards scowls. “Flag burning should be punishable by a good flogging!”

title: Operation Failed
text: Dr. Henri Jacquil made the headlines yesterday after a mistake made during a routine operation caused the death of your Minister of Foreign Affairs. With the recent advances in the capabilities of artificial intelligence, some in the medical field are wondering if autonomous robot surgeons should be given a whack at surgery.
chosen_option_text: “Why stop at just the operating room doors when there’s so much more an AI could do for us?” asks Dr. Elizabeth Kamen, Professor of Experimental Gynaecological Robotics, fetching a fresh box of batteries from the top shelf. “We could make hospitals so much more efficient if we allowed them to adopt more roles: diagnostic chatbots, robot nurses, computerised counsellors, and so on. AIs should outnumber humans by at least twenty to one on the hospital staff.”

title: Foetal Furore
text: Video coverage of a protest outside of an abortion clinic has gone viral after the footage indicated that pro-life campaigners prevented ingress of pregnant women, causing the patients visible distress. In response, the Womyn’s Liberation League has pushed for a bill that it says would protect access to clinics.
chosen_option_text: “What about the right to free speech?” pleads Yoshi Ratican, lawyer for the pro-life activists depicted in the footage. “These are public spaces, and my clients should have the freedom, as well as the ability, to get their views across. You may disagree with them, but it would be draconian for the government to prohibit their citizens from revealing to people the truth about any medical procedure they are getting.”

title: Flooding the Market
text: Recent floods devastated low-lying areas, and the affected areas are only just starting to recover. Now, news is emerging that during the disaster many local retailers were found to have significantly elevated prices for basic necessities such as water, blankets, flashlights, and matsutake mushrooms.
chosen_option_text: “Power to the People! Potatoes for the Proletariat!” chants pro-communalist speaker Nefertiti Simpson, whose father is said to own half of Emu County. “I ask you, why isn’t the government mass-producing and storing long-life foodstuffs, in order to distribute them for free during times of crisis and national emergency?”

title: The One-Trick Pony
text: Secretariat, a horse recently elected as mayor of Emu City, has been vetoing every single bill coming into his office, sternly shouting “Neigh!” every time.
chosen_option_text: “Meow!” trills Ms. Snuggleworth, pushing off all the papers on your desk aside from a bill proposing her ‘Animal Personhood (Except Icky Dogs)’ agenda be made policy nationwide. Purring persuasively, she curls up in your lap.

title: Everyone Loves Shipping
text: Since their invention, globally standardised shipping containers have been critical to facilitating international trade, allowing for the easy transfer of goods between different modes of transport. However, for some time Vanilla Llama has had a strongly negative trade balance — that is, it imports far more than it exports. This has led to a domestic surplus of these containers, with thousands of the steel boxes endlessly accumulating outside ports and freight terminals.
chosen_option_text: “Nobody is coming to pick these containers up, so we need to fill them, and filling them means fixing that trade deficit,” counsels business analyst Brett Onwards, who has spent all morning trying to sell homemade cookies to your staff. “We need to re-gear our economy towards manufacturing and export production. That means using subsidies to push these industries up, funded with tariffs on imported goods. As the trade balance corrects, our metal mountain will move offshore.”

title: Video Games Too Violent, Say Parents
text: Recently, there has been an enormous commercial success for ‘violent’ video games such as ‘Blood ‘n’ Guts 2: The Revenge’, ‘Tremor’, and ‘Grand Theft Tricycle’. Several parents’ groups have been calling for tougher restrictions on these games.
chosen_option_text: “Why not rate games the same way we rate movies?” asks Norman Larkin, a spokesperson for the Vanilla Llama Censorship Board. “We could give each game a content rating based on age appropriateness, and add descriptors on the box explaining why the game gets a certain rating. A little funding and we can stop children getting violent video games without affecting all the older ‘gamers’. Everyone will be happy. Except tax payers, I guess.”

title: You’ve Got a Friend in Bee
text: Honeybee populations have been decreasing at an alarming rate, according to a recent study published in Not That Popular Science magazine. Experts have swarmed your office demanding you take action or face catastrophic consequences.
chosen_option_text: “Whatever happened to leaving nature alone?” queries the eccentric ‘Doctor Bees’, carrying suitcases buzzing with bees and seen wearing a full bee costume. “More bee colonies? Pesticides? Genes? Buzz off! Have you ever stopped to think that we are to blame for this mess? Why don’t we free the bees and let nature take its course? Sure, the beekeeping industry would suffer, but if we do nothing the alternative is total environmental disaster! Buzz buzz buzz!”

title: Born to Be My Baby
text: When Moiraine Rose and her husband couldn’t conceive, they employed a surrogate to bear a child for them, using the father’s sperm and the surrogate mother’s egg. However, after the baby was born, the surrogate mother refused to give up the child and is battling for permanent custody.
chosen_option_text: “That’s a terrible idea. Nobody should put baby in a corner!” grumbles RuPaul Franco, the director of Vanilla Llama City Minimum Security Orphanarium, cradling a baby in his arms, while two other toddlers clutch at his clothes. “Our institution is overflowing with poor orphans. Wouldn’t it be better if you just provided financial incentives, perhaps paid for with a small tax increase, for infertile couples to adopt?” Taking advantage of your momentary absent-mindedness, he puts the baby on your lap. “Speaking of adoption, would you like to take care of this adorable little girl? I think she likes you.”

title: A Midsummer Night’s Snooze-Fest
text: As legions of interns scramble to set up a stage in your office, your Minister of Theatrics dramatically announces that her Ministry has organized a play for you. The play purportedly tells a tragic story: the public apathy toward the long-dead but highly-influential Vanilla Llaman playwright Bill Wakesword.
chosen_option_text: An intern apparently playing the part of ‘unenthusiastic teenager’ pokes the Minister with a smartphone, causing him to crumble to the floor in mock agony. The intern robotically states, “Alas. Poor Wakesword. I knew him well. I would have surely been willing to get interested in Wakesword if his word choice was easier. If only we could rework Wakesword so that it appealed to me, a disaffected teenager, and my social media habits.”

title: Licensing Driving Vanilla Llamen Crazy
text: Your cousin arrived at your office this afternoon, out of breath and deeply frustrated at having to spend day after day filling out forms, only to wait for six hours in a queue to register for another appointment to receive his 27B/6 form to finalize his registration and legally drive the sweet new ride he bought six weeks ago. You’ve agreed, after some persuasion, to hold a meeting with your Minister of Transportation and other experts to look into streamlining the process.
chosen_option_text: “I have a radical idea,” announces Yolanda Schultz, the CEO of Vanilla Llama’s largest automobile manufacturer. “Simply license car dealerships to handle these processes for consumers! We can fill out all the necessary insurance paperwork for car owners, and even issue driving permits! The DMV is only slow because it has no competition. If dealerships can compete with one another for the best service, buying and registering a new car won’t be such a frustrating ordeal!”

title: “Partisanship Too Far?” Wrongly Asks Opposition
text: After a recent incident where a lifeguard refused to save a drowning swimmer because she thought he looked like he belonged to another political party, talking heads on cable TV have seized upon the moment to ask if the current partisan political tensions in Vanilla Llama have gotten out of control.
chosen_option_text: “I don’t see what the problem is,” notes your aide, turning off your TV. “In fact, I say we enhance partisan identification by designating what colors people can wear based on their political affiliation. Then you’ll immediately know who is working to better the country, and who only has morally bankrupt and wrongheaded ideas.”

title: Parliamentary Playground
text: After a WhoTube video featuring MPs in an outright brawl went viral, foreign commentators now regularly mock the hijinks in the Vanilla Llaman Parliament. In order to save face, several MPs have tried to rein in the legislature’s embarrassing behavior.

title: Siren Song

title: Jolly Roger Sighted Off the Port Bow!

title: A Capital City for Vanilla Llama?

text: Mobs of disgruntled employees picket fast-food chains across Vanilla Llama, tossing cheeseburgers at customers and burning their uniforms — all in the name of dignity and fairer wages.

title: Warning, Fatigue
text: A recent midnight explosion at the Vanilla Llaman National Steelworks, which claimed nine lives and injured a dozen more, was found to be due to an easily fixable error. title: Famous Rapper Going South?

title: A Dread Letter

title: Bet Your Life

title: Betting on the Future

title: Fake News, Everyone!

title: Let Freedom Ring

title: Nazi Sympathizers Plan Rally

title: Parking Hell
text: The new director of the Vanilla Llama City Department of Transportation has suggested that imposing dynamic parking prices might help ease the city centre’s nightmarish congestion. Because the national government owns large parts of the capital, the plan cannot proceed without your approval.

title: A Question of Bad Faith
text: The Movementarians, the infamous cult associated with a mass suicide in the United Federation, has expressed interest in purchasing a vacant plot of land in Vanilla Llama. title: A Blast From the Past
text: A teacher and four schoolchildren were killed on a field trip in a remote region of Vanilla Llama after an old anti-personnel mine was accidentally detonated. The landmines - relics of the nation’s previous wars - have taken the lives of many over the years.

title: Stop Training and Start Coaching
text: A feasibility study into railway lines in the boondocks of Vanilla Llama has suggested that they are economically unsustainable. title: Vanilla Llama Falls Flat in Singing Contest
text: Last night, in the finals of popular reality TV contest Land of Faceplacevision, the Vanilla Llaman representative lost, despite giving what almost all critics in Vanilla Llama have declared to be a superior performance. title: Support Your Local Arms Manufacturer
text: After the Conglomerated Vanilla Llaman Arms Syndicate announced yet another setback in the development of a promised new fighter jet, the Hell-Emu 3000, the Ministry of Defense is considering the previously unthinkable: importing from overseas.

title: Citizens Struggle Under “Unfair” Tax Burden

title: Maternity Leave a Must, Say Mothers

title: Toss the Coin?
text: A recent financial crisis has seen the currency of East Lebatuck plummet, making that nation a popular holiday destination for Vanilla Llamen. chosen_option_text: “If you allow this fraud to continue, I’ll go bankrupt!” yells Agnes Rogers, the owner of the Eckie-Cola Company, emptying her pockets and scattering dozens of East Lebatuckese coins on your desk. “These marauders have come back from holiday and literally plundered our coin-operated vending machines. title: Opening the Door to Controversy
text: Actor Piers Hill, the famously tweedy star of superhero franchise Superbloke, has been heavily criticised after an incident at a Shop-Qwik, in which he was accused of “holding back women’s rights by holding open doors”.

title: Loose Lips, Characters Shipped?
text: In what has become the latest cultural controversy to strike Vanilla Llama, the highly anticipated series finale of the long-running fantasy cartoon show Time Adventure saw two of the protagonist’s main male companions share a brief, romantic kiss, confirming a decade’s worth of rumors surrounding their relationship. title: Your Wild Self(ie)
text: A nature photographer on assignment in the Kawandalandian wilderness caught an emu toying with their spare camera equipment. Either on purpose or by accident, this emu managed to snap a selfie. chosen_option_text: “Whether Vanilla Llaman or beast, we are promoting a culture of selfishness and unchecked narcissism,” complains self-styled intellectual and motivational speaker Kanya Putin. “I don’t know where this is going to lead us, but it won’t be anything good.
