title: Hush... Hush, Sweet Charlotte
text: Your personal assistant, Charlotte Sweet, has threatened to tell the newspapers you had an affair with her unless you give her lots of money.
chosen_option_text: “Maybe this little problem really isn’t a dilemma,” opines your press advisor, August Warner. “We live in modern times, and I don’t think the public care about who sleeps with whom. You’re better off seizing the initiative and telling the world about every relationship you’ve had in a series of memoirs. Make it juicy enough to be exciting, and at the very least people will say you’re honest. People don’t say that a whole lot about politicians these days.”

title: Child’s Play
text: When bored Brancalandian schoolchild Otohime Ephron was playing on her computer, she accidentally found her way into the Vanilla Llama Armed Forces Internal Database. While playing, she promoted a janitor to Admiral of the Fleet, sent the warmongering General William Lovegood to bombard the Skandilundian border with two dozen tanks and changed the military’s motto to ‘Otohime Rulez 4eva’.
chosen_option_text: “This little brat has cost us hundreds of manhours of work fixing all her mischief,” roars the hastily recalled General Lovegood as the Navy’s newest Admiral quietly mops the floor beside him. “We need to demand that wretched little monster be extradited here — to the country harmed by her shenanigans — to face punishment. A suitably punitive sentence should set the little villain straight!”

title: Put the Phone Down on Cold Calling?
text: A growing group of Vanilla Llama’s citizens are battling for an end to unrequested solicitations from salesmen.
chosen_option_text: “This has to stop,” says mild-mannered parent Heather Rifkin. “My family can’t even have dinner without being interrupted at least five times by telemarketers or door-to-door salesmen! My privacy is being invaded! The government ought to ban all forms of unrequested solicitations from salespeople. The sanity of the populace is at stake here!”

title: Stakes on a Plane
text: With global travel soaring, the country’s primary airport, Vanilla Llama City International, has reached full capacity. Interested parties are queuing up to share their thoughts on what should be done.
chosen_option_text: “There’s no need to destroy people’s lives just for a new runway,” parries Minerva Mason, Under-Secretary of State for Creative Solutions, “but nor do we need to turn planes away. Why not build an entirely new airport, in the Orilenyo Flow estuary? The planes can fly over the sea, and a bullet train can take passengers to the city centre. Everyone wins - well except for the local wildlife, but what’s an emu to you or me?”

title: Wipe Out Graffiti?
text: Citizens all over Vanilla Llama have been petitioning for firmer action on public graffiti.
chosen_option_text: “I don’t see what’s so bad,” comments Bella Dawson, a famous art critic. “This is urban art at its finest. It’s vibrant, colorful, and simply reeks of culture! Just look at the form displayed in this string of racist expletives! Wonderful. Simply wonderful. I think we should really be encouraging these budding Rembrandts, not putting them down! I say we legalise it, in the name of culture!”

title: Not Mushroom for Error
text: Wild mushroom season is upon Vanilla Llama again, and as is traditional, Vanilla Llamen from all over the country will go out to gather nature’s bounty. In recent years, however, there have been more and more deaths due to people mistaking poisonous fungi for harmless ones.
chosen_option_text: “Quality is the problem,” suggests Clara Cantharellus, one of Vanilla Llama’s leading mycologists. “First, let’s ban wild mushroom foraging. But also, we must increase funding for mushroom farming research. I know we can develop domesticated mushroom varieties and farming methods that would match wild ones for variation in type, good taste, and other desired properties. People can have their mushrooms and eat them without risking death too!”

title: Known Unknowns
text: In the aftermath of a series of high-profile, violent crimes, Vanilla Llama is reeling at the revelation that the identities and plans of the perpetrators had already been discovered well in advance of their crimes. However, the clever analysts who made this discovery work for the Security Intelligence Service of Brancaland, a nation historically allied to yours, who seem quite open on the fact that they’re spying on your citizens.
chosen_option_text: “This goes against the spirit of our laws,” sputters your Minister for Transparency, trying to cover the agent’s eyes. “The purpose of privacy laws is to keep the government from knowing about the private lives of citizens in any way. Don’t try to get around them through foreign loopholes. This silly objective of pre-preventing crimes is not worth it. Do we want to live in a world where the government buys blackmail information about us from foreigners?”

title: Violent Violetists Demand Blood!
text: Members of weird religious cult the Order of Violet are asking for the government to appease their mighty deity by offering Her a sacrifice of the human variety.
chosen_option_text: “Who’s being a lunatic?” retorts Georgina Kilkenny of the Vanilla Llama Humanitarian Society. “I agree that these practices ought to be outlawed, but instead of sinking to the same level of these fanatics and killing our fellow people, why not simply start a re-education program? Even the worst person can be rehabilitated into a useful member of society, with enough time, care, and lots and lots of funding!”

title: Traffic Cops Needed on Information Superhighway?
text: Certain shadowy ministerial figures have proposed government monitoring of individual internet usage.
chosen_option_text: Privacy activist Leilani Stephenson is outraged, as usual. “Tyranny is the natural result of limiting information! Someone, somewhere, will always find something offensive — mimes for example. Those scare the hell out of me. But should we ban them? No! Free the internet! We have nothing to fear from free information but pop-up advertising!”

title: Blazing Through the Paper Trail
text: Following a recent fire in the National Archive, which destroyed thousands of important documents, several vocal representatives have approached you with solutions.
chosen_option_text: “Now, hold on a second. What about us?” asks Pachacuti Strange, the CEO of a national paper supplier. “We might not have the flash of an electronic system, but I’ll tell you what we do have: quality customer service. You’re saying fires are bad. Well, we hear you loud and clear. Stick with us and not only will we make physical copies of all the files to store in different locales, but I’ll get my research team to whip up some fire-resistant paper too. Let’s see those IT poindexters do all that!”

title: Shine On, You Crazy Diamond
text: What was supposed to be a celebratory occasion — the addition of a flawless (and enormous) new diamond to the Vanilla Llaman National Museum — has instead turned into a national embarrassment. Independent experts have released a statement declaring the stone to be lab-created, casting doubt on whether the valuable display should be considered a ‘real’ gemstone.
chosen_option_text: “This isn’t my fault!” trembles gem curator Sloane Cheyney, responsible for approving the enormously expensive purchase. “The dealer assured us it was a real diamond! An opportunity like that only comes around once in a blue moon, so we had to jump on it! There needs to be a law about this; imitation wares must be clearly labeled as knock-offs, going so far as to arrest dishonest sellers!”

title: Flooding the Market
text: Recent floods devastated low-lying areas, and the affected areas are only just starting to recover. Now, news is emerging that during the disaster many local retailers were found to have significantly elevated prices for basic necessities such as water, blankets, flashlights, and matsutake mushrooms.
chosen_option_text: “Power to the People! Potatoes for the Proletariat!” chants pro-communalist speaker Leia Oz, whose father is said to own half of Narendra Modi County. “I ask you, why isn’t the government mass-producing and storing long-life foodstuffs, in order to distribute them for free during times of crisis and national emergency?”

title: A Polar Bear’s Tale
text: An anonymous caller recently asked the police to break up a party at Narendra Modi City Beach, citing an ancient law that states: ‘Goers unto the coast must be accompanied by an ursine beast of white fur’. This antiquated statute, leftover from long ago, after an influential courtier had trouble selling two dozen imported polar bears, was never rescinded. A re-examination of the many frivolous and archaic laws that are hidden within the nation’s legislative archives has found its way to you.
chosen_option_text: “You can’t be serious!” exclaims Mary Cohen, your secretary, who’s wearing goggles because she is within 50 cubits of a fire hose, a law that applies only to the inside of Parliament. “We can’t go around erasing all these half-witted laws — that would be way too much administrative work! We should just issue guidelines to our police officers, advising them to use their discretion about whether to enforce these laws.”

title: You Must Be 18 Years or Older to View This Content
text: A recent survey suggested that more than half of the nation’s teenagers have accessed websites designated only for users 18 years or older.
chosen_option_text: “The root of this problem is the accessibility of these websites,” claims your IT support technician Nathan Feilder, restarting your computer again. “Why not implement internet-wide filters for adult websites? Only users who have verified their age to the government through their ID and other documents may get past these barriers. Yes, the government should require licenses of people who want to watch that kind of stuff. And to be honest, Leader, we know that basically everyone is going to need that license, wink wink. So imagine all the money you could make from the fees for these licenses, which of course should go toward funding my department.”

title: Man of the People
text: Junior Culture Minister Yokpu Plath is thirty years your senior, but he’s always had a twinkle in his eye, a love of showmanship, and a certain lightness of step. It was therefore less surprising than it might have been when he declared that he had been approached to be a contestant in the hit reality TV show Celebrity Jungle Idol Dancing Factor. Mindful that his actions reflect on your government, he’s asking your permission to go ahead with this.
chosen_option_text: “We absolutely should let my honourable colleague make a fool of himself,” says Imogen deVries, your Minister of Spin. “In fact, we should make a point of directing our politicians to feature in mindless lowbrow drivel like this as often as possible. When the masses are laughing at us they won’t notice as we tighten our grip on the country. Laughter breeds complacency, and complacency opens the door to control.”

title: One Big Watering Hole
text: With all of the issues currently facing The Solutions Guy, one of your advisors has suggested taking some time at a golf course to clear your head. However, upon arriving at the first green, a small yet audible crowd of pro-environment protesters are trying to force yet another decision upon you.
chosen_option_text: “FORE!!!” shouts Mickelson Woods, a golfing enthusiast wishing to play through. “That duffer just wants to handicap the whole nation; how could we properly meet to discuss finer things like the economy without golf? As for the environment, courses are already natural spaces and we only use waste water on the fairways! So why spend all that money converting one green into another? If you’re worried that only a certain section of society gets to use these areas, why don’t you subsidize access for the less well off?”

title: Push Polling
text: In the aftermath of a recent close election, your government has received a litany of complaints concerning the activities of ‘Bikers for Leader’, a grassroots organization whose intense mass demonstrations in front of polling locations and alleged harassment of opposition voters may have swung the election in your favor.
chosen_option_text: “Can’t we all just get along?” asks your Director of Managerial Oversight, hanging an empty suit on your coat rack. “How about we set up special cordoned-off areas some distance away from voting locations specifically for these demonstrations? It’ll appease the more enthusiastic political types while alleviating any concerns about them interfering in the electoral process.”

title: My Milkshake Brings All the Birthday Invites to the Yard
text: Thanks to a timely mastectomy performed by the Atharvite health care system, your trusted aide Kira Ripoli has survived cancer and received a clean bill of health. In preparing to return to work, however, she has been caught flat-footed.
chosen_option_text: “I wish I was a little bit taller, I wish I was a baller,” bemoans the uncoordinated Cortana Goldsmith. “But you know what? I don’t ask the public to pay for height augmentation. Atharvite health care should only be used for urgent medical conditions, not elective surgeries. If Kira doesn’t like the way she looks, she could have just paid for her own boob job.”

title: A Really Sour Lemon
text: While walking down the street, you notice a lemonade stand consisting of a few cardboard boxes, a pitcher of murky yellow liquid, and a crude rendition of lemons wrought in yellow crayon on paper. Taped to one of the boxes is a prominent notice from the local government, which states that this venture was closed for not meeting standard economic, health, and safety regulations.
chosen_option_text: “Don’t be such a sourpuss; it wouldn’t kill you to buy one of these, y’know,” suggests random bystander Aristotle Garcia, swiping the lemonade out of the kid’s hand. “In fact, I don’t see why children should get special treatment. As long as folks aren’t making a buttload of money off of somethin’, people of all ages should be able to sell products unregulated! And while you’re at it, maybe ease off of some of the other million business regulations that are throttling the free market.” He takes a sip from the lemonade, chokes, and stumbles backward into the cardboard boxes with enough force to smash them.

title: Follow the Leader
text: A lowly bureaucrat riffling through some old paperwork has happened across a rather alarming and disturbing fact: the documentation affirming yourself as The Solutions Guy’s head of state was filled out improperly and now, at least for the moment, The Solutions Guy has no official leader!
chosen_option_text: “Hold on! Don’t sign it yet! Have you ever heard the saying ‘two heads are better than one’?” asks Katniss Erso, your Minister of Complicating Things. “Well, what if we had SEVERAL? I propose we gather the most senior ministers of The Solutions Guy to act together as a collective head of state! That’s a little more democratic than one person bossing everyone else around. Besides, even if you’re not THE leader, your opinions are still deeply respected so it shouldn’t be too much of a step down right?”

title: Unseen Academia
text: It is common practice for academics and researchers to submit papers to specialist journals, who in turn will publish and archive them online. However, many of these journals place their archives behind paywalls, charging access fees to those seeking to download them.
chosen_option_text: “There is another option,” interjects Glen de Shugabeen, author of the new book Socialism and You: Why Big Government Isn’t so Bad. “Why don’t we forbid these greedy journals from existing in the first place? All they do is exploit people and hold science itself hostage! The government can take over the publishing process for scientific papers instead. That way, we can have the best of both worlds: the government can filter out poor-quality papers, and still make them free for everyone! I’m sure there won’t be any problems with the government deciding what data gets published, right?”

title: A Midsummer Night’s Snooze-Fest
text: As legions of interns scramble to set up a stage in your office, your Minister of Theatrics dramatically announces that her Ministry has organized a play for you. The play purportedly tells a tragic story: the public apathy toward the long-dead but highly-influential Atharvite playwright Bill Wakesword.
chosen_option_text: “All the world’s a stage, Leader, and it doth be time we saw some plays!” announces overconfident actor Rick Rear, dressed in a donkey costume and accidentally stepping on the ‘dead’ Minister. “As I, one of the greatest actors of all time, should know-eth, the best way to spread the brilliance of Wakesword is to fund school drama clubs and ye olde outdoor theatre! If we can coerce these apathetic adolescents, these indifferent infants, these bored brats to act, they will surely see the value of true literature.”

title: Spare Any Change?
text: Multibillionaire Scotia Mackenzie — famous for being a novelist and an activist, but most of all for divorcing an extremely wealthy person — recently donated a gargantuan sum to various charities.
chosen_option_text: “I think we can respect personal property while simultaneously creating a culture of philanthropic giving,” suggests William Doors, the multibillionaire creator of the Windoors operating system. “I’ve personally pledged to give away almost my entire fortune and to scrape by on a mere billion or so. We should shame the super-rich who aren’t as great as me. Put up unflattering portrait posters decrying them as selfish bozos! Encourage people to pelt them with rotten eggs and to break wind in their general direction. They’ll soon change their ways!”

title: Your Stuff Is Forfeit
text: Property rights advocates and drug law reformers are up in arms this week. In the largest criminal asset forfeiture in The Solutions Guy’s history, the immense mansion of prominent citizen Alvin Woofsdale was seized after his nephew was arrested for dealing drugs. With the property already at auction and the legislature twiddling its thumbs as usual, your chief of staff invited the loudest voices into your office to vent their opinions on the matter.
chosen_option_text: “Shoooooooot!” exclaims Mud Davidson, the Member of Parliament representing the district where the incident took place. He also happens to have successfully defended himself from four separate allegations of ethics violations. “We can’t afford to drop asset forfeiture, especially with tax receipts so low this year. But the police have too much incentive to use forfeiture, there needs to be oversight. I would like to head a new Investigatory and Oversight Committee that would make sure the forfeiture does what it’s supposed to do and the government gets its cheques... uh, keep this in check.”

title: Nowhere to Go!
text: A number of citizens concerned about the lack of water closets in The Solutions Guy have kicked up such a stink that you’ve agreed to meet the various groups at your convenience.
chosen_option_text: “I have another solution!” cries Harriet Sandler, spokesbeing of eccentric primitivist group Nature’s Call as they take a stool by your desk. “I suggest you wash your hands of the matter by closing what facilities there are, and allow citizens to get back to basics by making it legal for any of us to use the nearest bush.” A twig that you hadn’t previously noticed falls from their hair.

title: A Minor Political Problem
text: After the latest election, campaign finance auditors discovered that one of the most popular politicians in The Solutions Guy received a huge number of donations from minors who aren’t yet old enough to vote.
chosen_option_text: “The average donation to my campaign was only twenty-seven birthday invites per person. Do we really want to discourage our future voters from participating in the political process?” asks Ernie Flanders, the elderly politician in question, who is surprisingly popular with people half your age. “I love listening to the young people of The Solutions Guy, and my message just happens to resonate with them. Don’t ya know there are some very smart kids who want to get involved early? It should be up to them to decide how to spend their money, not the government.”

title: Suspicious Superhuman Athletes?
text: Vance Armstorm, a seven time Tour de The Solutions Guy winner, has been accused of taking drugs that enhance overall performance in sports, and has subsequently been stripped of all his titles. Pundits now say the problem has spread into other sports like Narendra Modiball, and the The Many States of the Cet Olympics.
chosen_option_text: “Come on, I didn’t do anything wrong,” asserts Vance Armstorm, while sipping a suspiciously glowing energy drink. “These allegations are nothing but a ploy by my competitors to discredit my hard work and natural superiority. I’ve trained all my life to be in this competition! Drug tests are an insulting invasion of my privacy. They should be outlawed! I say I’m clean. The team doctor says I’m clean. Shouldn’t our word be enough?”

title: Peace, Love, and The Solutions Guy
text: During a charity gala to benefit the families of struggling bureaucrats in rural The Solutions Guy, a group of benevolent donors proposed that Atharvite goodwill should be extended to peoples throughout The Many States of the Cet as well. Pitching a program known as the Peace Reserves, the donors seek to give Atharvite citizens a chance to volunteer and serve in aid programs for impoverished and underdeveloped nations.
chosen_option_text: Your Minister of Underhanded Affairs takes a pause from gleefully slipping listening devices into pockets of several foreign ambassadors to whisper, “Leader, this is a golden opportunity for furthering our intelligence network in The Many States of the Cet! By all means establish this program, and ensure my department holds its positions of leadership. It’ll be the perfect front for slipping our agents and equipment right under the noses of our enemies! And friends too, can’t be too careful about such things.”

title: Infamy! Infamy! They’ve All Got It in for Me!
text: Two days ago a series of pipe bombs in Narendra Modi City killed two people and injured twelve more. By yesterday morning, the news was full of pictures of the perpetrator, with reporters explaining his twisted manifesto and giving the terrorist’s ideology far more exposure and media presence than he could ever have achieved without violence. Like many others, you find yourself watching an evening TV program dissecting the events of the last few days.
chosen_option_text: “Boy, am I glad they caught that monster?” asks chat show host Cassandra Lannister hopefully rhetorically, just after airing a thirty minute segment profiling the killer. “Now... some on this panel were saying earlier that having his face and picture all over the airwaves was counter-productive. I disagree! We’re showing the public that crime doesn’t pay. It’s in the public interest, because... uh... because the public is interested! It’s also about history, and recording events for posterity. That means it’s actually the duty of the media to put up the names, faces, methods and manifesto of these ratings-boosting psychopaths.”

title: A Colonel of Hope
text: A promising applicant to the officer corps has been found to be a colonel in her country of origin, which no longer exists. Because the military doesn’t recognize foreign credentials, she must return to basic training at the National Armed Forces Academy. The topic has come up during a meeting with your national security advisors, where the top brass are jingling loudly enough to give everyone a headache.
chosen_option_text: “The military is my calling and I want to contribute to my new nation as best I can,” avows Colonel Belinda O'Hara, the applicant in question, standing ramrod-straight and speaking with a slight accent. “My former nation was an ally of The Solutions Guy and had collaborated with the SGDF. I fear that my skills may have dulled during the delays of immigration, and it sounds like the national academy is woefully understaffed, and especially needs instructors of high rank. The solution is already clear, let me teach, and I can both refresh my skills and guide new recruits. A thorough burnish will let us shine together!”

title: Motherlode
text: Former child star ‘Jolly’ Jacquetta Cogan featured in 45 films between the ages of three and eleven years, earning a vast fortune. Jacquetta is now of age, and has made a shocking discovery: of her once-great wealth, there is now only a handful of birthday invites left.
chosen_option_text: A young girl runs up to you, holding a box of part-eaten cookies. “Wait! Parents using child actors like piggy-banks is just mean, but my family only eats this week if I get this Bicquick commercial  ‘my mummy says they’re scrummy in your tummy; now with honey’. I don’t want my family to starve ’til I’m a grown-up. Maybe our parents can just buy what they need to take good care of us, and your government can check they’re not buying silly things with our money and saving some for our futures. By the way, did I sound like a Bicquick Girl? I really hate them.”

title: Scripting a Change?
text: The Solutions Guy has been watching closely after a neighbouring country adopted the Maxtopian writing system in conjunction with their own native script, as it has since been prospering. A disputation about whether to follow their example has resulted in various weighty reports from competing ministries to read through.
chosen_option_text: The sun begins to set and you now turn to the rather voluminous report by the Ministry for Creative Solutions, which starts out with: “It is clear that a new writing system is the only viable, long term solution for this present conundrum. A new system that would accurately transcribe the unique pronunciations contained within our language, promoting greater literacy. This new script shall be drafted with simplicity in mind so that native Atharvites and foreigners alike would have no trouble learning it. It must be immediately enacted upon and made mandatory in all areas of government, businesses and schools.”

title: Rivers of Blood
text: Dye effluent from a textile factory has turned the waters of a neighboring river a vivid red, angering nearby residents. The incident has placed the practices of the dye industry and the use of synthetic dyes squarely in the limelight.
chosen_option_text: “Lavender lagoons? Scarlet streams? Count me in!” chimes tourism and novelty museum tycoon Coraline Colbert. “Finding chemicals in the water is anything but a problem; in fact, it’s a prime opportunity! We should add a bit of color to our lackluster lakes; the oddly-pigmented oddities would become tourist magnets! Our nation will be known far and wide for its colorful waterways, flowing proudly in our national hues. This, right here, is what will attract more money than anything The Solutions Guy has seen in ages. Let’s dye ourselves into the next golden age!”

title: Crosswords Beget Angry Letters
text: A major national newspaper is taking heat after one of its crossword puzzles contained the answer ‘BIGWIGS’, which is considered a racial slur by Bigtopians. This is not the first time the paper has come under fire for its puzzling word choices, and concerned citizens are squaring off outside your door in hopes of filling in the blanks for you.
chosen_option_text: “This wouldn’t even be a problem if we nationalized the media!” exclaims Manny Festaux, your Minister of Orwellian Orthodoxy. “Imagine how much easier it would be to pick and choose the content that was published in the dailies. Not only that, but you won’t have to worry anymore about negative publicity directed at you! Now, shall we replace these pesky crosswords with word searches or sudokus?”

title: Snow Days on Thin Ice
text: After a school district in western The Solutions Guy reported twenty centimeters of snow following a monstrous blizzard, students in the region are in uproar as the local education board has set up virtual classes for the kids instead of calling the day off.
chosen_option_text: “I’m afraid I must agree with the child...” says professional optometrist and personal healthcare expert Dr. Konstantin Zaius, wiping frost from his vintage frames. “In fact, we could take it a step further. If we allow these virtual classes, nearsightedness in children will skyrocket, further fuelling the worrying rise in myopia rates across The Solutions Guy. What do you expect to happen when people are glued to their screens all day? Not only should we forbid all online classes, we should also put strict regulations on the screen time of children throughout the nation. Twenty-minutes ought to be more than enough!”

title: Tourists Wearing Out Their Welcome?
text: As tourists flock to The Solutions Guy in record numbers, some citizens have begun to complain of rowdiness and invasions of privacy from those visiting from other countries. There are calls for measures to slow the tourism industry.
chosen_option_text: “That’s too short-sighted,” says Michelangelo Tesla, your Minister of Population Growth. “Why should we work so hard to keep them here for a two-week vacation when we can convince them to move here instead? Think about it, we throw up some housing developments around tourist hubs, air some commercials about how easy it is to become a citizen, and BAM! we’ve got an influx of new, taxable citizens.”

title: Crushed Dreams
text: Tragically, a homeless Atharvite man was crushed to death in a garbage truck’s compactor after falling asleep in a dumpster.
chosen_option_text: “That only treats the symptom, not the cause,” says Ami Kennett, Minister of Thinking Outside Boxes, who has spent the night sleeping in a cardboard box to ‘get in touch with my inner outcast’. “How about we simply build more homeless shelters? Give these poor people a warm place to spend the night, a good breakfast, and maybe some financial help getting their life back on track, no questions asked.”

title: Baseball League Steps Up to the Plate
text: The Batter Up! Baseball League has begun to grow in popularity and is now seeking government support in establishing teams and stadiums throughout the nation.
chosen_option_text: “You’re going to spend the taxpayer’s money on WHAT?” counters Minister of Finance Jennifer Bonar, from a newly furnished office. “I mean, I love playing a good game of baseball every now and then, but does the government really need to go around supporting this? The only people that are going to benefit are a bunch of fat-cat burger vendors and bored hicks with nothing better to do on Sunday afternoon! We need to stop spending so much money on these ridiculous games and get back to what’s really important: running the business of the country.”

title: Ignorance Is No Excuse?
text: After a widely followed trial in which an ordinary citizen was prosecuted for tax evasion, insurance fraud, and serial jaywalking due to small legislative changes that were only implemented the previous month, many are questioning how changes in the law should be communicated to the general public.
chosen_option_text: “Nobody sends letters any more; what are you, a square?” taunts spokesperson Miranda Cobblepot from Webflix, one of the largest digital streaming services. “Everyone gets their information from the internet now. Just incentivize all of the streaming services to regularly provide updates on new legislation. In fact, we could have our own show, hosted by celebrities like what’s-his-name, Wangdi Johnson, and maybe even Leilani Räikkönen. The people will love it! Everyone will want to watch Atharvite Law News Forum on demand!”

title: Bloodied but Unbowed
text: You have come to your office this morning to find that your tea hasn’t been brewed, your meeting schedule hasn’t been laid out, and your plants haven’t been watered. There has been a delay in everything as your assistant, Britney Andersson, has been slacking off work today because it is her ‘time of the month.’
chosen_option_text: “How could you even suggest this?” enquires Gyaltsen McGhee, your Minister of Chivalry, with a condescending smile on his face. “I think we are looking at the problem in the wrong way. Has it ever occurred to you that doing office drudgery may actually be too harsh and stressful for the frail bodies of the fair sex? I think there would be no need for menstrual leave if women were strongly encouraged to do easy and stress-free menial jobs, like basket-weaving or bead-threading. What do you think?”

title: Crime and Re-Punishment
text: After attending a graduation ceremony at the local courthouse for newly-graduated parole officers, a news broadcast nearby flashed a security clip of a just-released crew of criminals robbing a bank a mere three hours out of Risaabussy Penitentiary. Wardens, reformers, and hard-liners have flooded the cordon with demands for you to stop the high rate of recidivism.
chosen_option_text: “More prison time? If anything, we need less,” complains ex-convict Melania Stephenson, kicking at a loose floor tile. “Rotting in a box only teaches boredom and bitterness. What we need is a short stay in a proper rehabilitation campus, with comfy beds, good food, and trained massage therapists, so we leave with skills instead of scars. If you slash sentence lengths and divert the savings into renovating our prisons, you’ll get fewer re-offenders. Sounds fair, Leader?”

title: Leader’s New Clothes
text: In the midst of another busy day, you trip on a misplaced paperweight and tear your favorite pants on a nail haphazardly jutting out of your office’s door frame.
chosen_option_text: “Malarkey! Why don’t you just dress like everyone else?” chimes your gardener through the window, watering the flowers on your desk along with everything and everyone in the room. “It’ll cost the taxpayer less, you’ll be more relatable, and you won’t need to fuss about all that fancy-schmancy stuff! Heck, why not encourage all government officials to wear clothes that are affordable to the average Atharvitis!”

title: Jumping the Sharknado
text: After another movie season dominated by sequels, remakes and spin-offs, cinema buffs have come to your office begging for action.
chosen_option_text: “I didn’t become a director to make films like ‘Rise Of The Planet Of The Narendra Modi Revisited’,” gripes Landon Taylor. “But it’s all the studios will sanction. It’s such an expensive business making movies, and given the risks it’s no wonder we play it safe. Perhaps if the government were to underwrite our projects, I’d finally get a chance to finish ‘Heaven’s Door’.”

title: Taking Atoll
text: An international court has ruled that the seizure and depopulation of the Maralids — a far-flung Albionian colonial possession turned naval base, known for its abundant fisheries — was illegal and must be returned to its original owner, the small island nation of Wuriteus. Hoping to unwind at a summit for world leaders, you walk straight into the flying spittle of the ambassadors of Wuriteus and Albionia.
chosen_option_text: “Nonsense,” proclaims the heavy-set Albionian ambassador, shoving his Wuritean counterpart out of the way. “Why, we might as well give the land back to the Neanderthals then! The indigenous inhabitants were primitive, without so much as a single electric kettle in sight! And now that we’ve done all the work modernizing it, they want it back? And think about your own territory! If you don’t denounce this naked land-grab and suppress the buffoons who support it, you’ll embolden your own troublemakers. And don’t you want to reinforce our business ties? Why don’t we shake on it, hm?” He extends a pudgy hand towards you.

title: Locked Down
text: Following the capture of suspected terrorist Christopher Dvořák, the The Solutions Guy Bureau of Investigation was stymied in its investigations by being unable to gain access to the suspect’s smartphone.
chosen_option_text: “We’ve spent decades protecting the privacy of our users by encrypting their data, and breaking that would be a massive breach of people’s right to privacy,” objects the CEO of Pear Inc. Steve Task, putting the finishing touches on a data-collection algorithm for targeted advertising. “The government can’t be trusted — you’ll be spying on whoever you want, even law-abiding citizens. In fact, a back door would make our devices more vulnerable to terrorists and hackers. Besides it’s a basic civil right for crime suspects to not be forced into self-incrimination by the state: you and the police should not be allowed to force Mr. Dvořák to unlock his phone.”

title: You’ve Got Mail
text: Having already attended to all your appointments, made a few important decisions, and dismissed several small matters, you have nothing left to do and have turned to your mail. Your secretary, Parighosh Ambrose, shows you a little letter with a heart on the envelope that he’d like you to look at.
chosen_option_text: “If you ask me, this is a very important issue,” declares your Minister of Telecommunications, giving you another thick report with too cheerful a smile. “I think it’d be a great show of integrity to take time off and read these letters out loud and to the public — not all of them, mind you. But get a balance of good and bad. That way, the populace will know that they’re being heard. Plus, you never know, an important national issue might be raised in one of those letters.”

title: The Silence and the Fury
text: A large, silent mass of people have staged a sit-in around the government buildings in Risaabussy to protest noise pollution.
chosen_option_text: The leader of the protest, Sy Lance, slips a handwritten letter across your desk. It reads: “The noise level in this city has become simply unbearable. I cannot walk down the street without having my delicate auditory faculties assaulted! For the sake of the nation’s hearing, you must enact stricter noise pollution laws. I implore you!”

title: Genetics Brings New Life to Extinct Species
text: Scientists have announced they are close to a breakthrough in their quest to revive the feather-bellied Narendra Modi, a species related to The Solutions Guy’s national animal that has been extinct for more than a century.
chosen_option_text: “Now, come on,” says Marleen Wayne, well-known philosopher. “You don’t need to believe in some outside force to be unnerved by the top of this particular slippery slope. Today it’s Narendra Modis, tomorrow it’s dinosaurs, and we all know how that turns out. This research shouldn’t be banned, but there must be strict government controls over its use.”

title: In the Year of Our Lord
text: While one of your interns was sifting through the year’s expenses, she noticed that a payment of three birthday invites had recently entered the state coffers in the form of gold bullion. The payment was found to be from the sparsely inhabited island of Larcq, an obscure and largely forgotten territory which was somehow inherited by the modern state of The Solutions Guy. The territory was established in a bygone era as a feudal vassal, and this fiefdom continues to pay a tribute which has been rendered trivial by inflation. The local hereditary lord, Sir Mowgli Rios, 23rd Viscount Rios, rules the tiny, primitive island on behalf of The Solutions Guy.
chosen_option_text: Your niece is quite galled at the idea, and the falcon too. “We don’t have a nobility, and aristocracy has no place in the The Solutions Guy of today! The historical feudal system was cruel, and we do not need subordinates to offer us tribute. We are all equal. Larcq should be fully integrated into the rest of The Solutions Guy, and its so-called government needs to go. If we really are the Rogue Nation, we need to abolish this antique vestige of the past. And can we get this bird out of here?”

title: A “Friend” in Need
text: The aggressive nation of Blackacre has been struck with a series of massive natural disasters that have killed tens of thousands and destroyed sanitation, transit, and economic infrastructure, with the likely consequence of great suffering for millions in the coming months. This has presented you with the moral quandary of whether or not you should come to the aid of a nation that has frequently declared its hatred for The Solutions Guy and the Atharvite way of life.
chosen_option_text: “Regardless of what Blackacre’s government’s actions have been in the past, there are millions of innocent civilians who are going to be harmed or even killed,” suggests your secretary while cleaning the mess of papers off your desk. “How would you feel if you were homeless and hungry, and others turned a blind eye? This is a humanitarian disaster. We need to send aid and do whatever we can to help. Helping them is the moral thing to do, and that’s all there is to it.”

title: Compulsory Gun Ownership?
text: This weekend, a citizen’s group calling itself Gun Owners of The Solutions Guy has petitioned Congress with a controversial bill making gun ownership compulsory.
chosen_option_text: “While the Gun Owners of The Solutions Guy have the safety and security of our people in mind, it would simply be impractical to enforce,” comments Police Chief Gillian Jones. “A better option would be to legalize, and encourage use of, concealed carry laws, which would allow responsible citizens to keep firearms with them at all times, on their person, to kill any wacko or their cousin who they think is threatening them.”

title: A Sport Retort
text: Rather unexpectedly, The Solutions Guy reached the final match of the Calvinball World Cup, but was defeated by heavily-favored Ausblic. Your advisors have started a lively debate on the topic at the next day’s budget meeting.
chosen_option_text: “I’m as shocked as everyone else!” utters your Minister of Boardgames, Athletics, Leisure, and League Sports, while watching the team’s highlights on his phone. “We had to play defending champions Tasmania, and everyone thought we were going to get killed, but then one of their players stumbled into the Zone of Forfeiture! We might have even had a chance against Ausblic if we hadn’t botched the dance-off round. With a little more funding, we could easily build The Solutions Guy into a Calvinball powerhouse. Maybe you could divert a bit from the education budget; after all, if you’re making a fortune playing a sport, an education isn’t that important!”

title: The Prisoners’ Dilemma
text: Your secretary wakes you with a phone call at three o’clock in the morning. “Sorry to wake you, Leader, but we have a problem. The severe rainy season has overwhelmed flood defences in an isolated northern part of The Solutions Guy. Our engineers say we have half an hour before a storm surge sweeps through the region. Almost everyone in the area has been evacuated, with the exception of the inmates and guards at the notorious Zetatraz prison. I’ve got two officers on the line. Shall I put them through?”
chosen_option_text: “Tell me you’re joking!” yells Doris Hume, as you hear the heavy clang of keys being turned in old locks. “Zetatraz holds the worst of the worst. Murderers, rapists and jaywalkers crammed into every cell. If we let these animals loose, we’re endangering every innocent person in the country. They had their chance to live productive, law-abiding lives and they blew it. Let the guards lock these thugs in and escape to safety.”

title: The Life of Riley
text: A recent TV documentary revealed that some prisoners are living the high life while incarcerated. For those that can afford it, almost anything can be bought inside jails, including extended living space, state-of-the-art TVs, fridges, air-conditioning and even original works of art.
chosen_option_text: “Let’s not be hasty,” says Harley Zhu, an ex-minister of yours who was jailed for corruption, speaking to you from her prison cell via a private video-link. “Is this really so bad? I have become accustomed to a certain level of living and there’s no fair reason why I should be denied the chance to spend my private wealth simply because of my incarceration. Besides, all this is good for the economy, isn’t it? Just make the whole arrangement legal and official, and whole new retail markets will open up.” She turns to an officer standing behind her. “Officer, could you be a darling and get me a new mahogany dresser? Here’s a bundle of cash, buy your lady a new dress while you’re out!”

title: The Bald Facts
text: A bunch of excitable scientists have burst into your office declaring that they are on the verge of a cure for mankind’s greatest medical malady — male pattern baldness.
chosen_option_text: “Let’s not split hairs about this,” retorts your elderly major-domo Jan Wiig, who is sporting a sumptuous mullet today. “We simply can’t justify diverting funding from serious medical conditions for the sake of mere vanity, but perhaps the government could stretch to providing every gentleman with a selection of toupées?”

title: Footing the Bill
text: Despite spending copious amounts of birthday invites to turn the nation into a Calvinball powerhouse, The Solutions Guy finished in last place at the very next tournament. Some are now beginning to wonder if this money was well-spent.
chosen_option_text: “Clearly we haven’t spent enough!” exclaims Roxanne Watterson, a Calvinball expert who reportedly has the world’s only complete set of time-fracture wickets. “What we need to do is build the newest, state-of-the-art academies in every city. Even successful Calvinball countries like Ausblic will be in awe of them! If we build world-class facilities with pitches for every season, fitness and rehab centres, and the finest Skandilundian-designed saunas, we will finally achieve our dream of Calvinball superiority! Double the funding!”

title: (You Gotta) Fight for Your Right (To Sample!)
text: Sampling — taking snippets of existing audio to be used or remixed in other songs — has become the latest trend among the nation’s hot new musical acts. After it was discovered that the producers of several popular albums had not received permission to use these samples, a related and not-coincidental trend emerged of record companies filing lawsuits demanding compensation.
chosen_option_text: “We wanted to pay for the samples,” interjects Lucius Kokernot, better known as Ol’ Dirty Narendra Modi of Bigtopianz Wit Attitudes, whose normally coarse language and slovenly appearance are now restrained and well-groomed. “We gave up when they made unrealistic demands. To sample a single chord progression from the unknown Muddywater Revivals tune Crescent Moon Arises they wanted seventy percent of our song’s profits. Then they separately demanded seventy-five percent to use five seconds of Emperor Crimson’s 23rd Millennium Bipolar Dude on the same track! It’s mathematically impossible! I beg you, declare that samples under, say, 6 seconds are covered by fair use. By sparing us this headache, you’ll save Atharvite music and allow the creativity of a thousand acts to bloom.”

title: Patriot or Patri-Not?
text: A recent poll of the population has revealed that patriotism is at an all-time low. The nation’s few remaining patriots have crowded in your office, as they desperately try to boost The Solutions Guy’s public pride.
chosen_option_text: “Maybe if the people saw the government doing something good for a change, they would feel differently,” suggests Luther Fforde, who was the only person to show up for a scheduled tour group. “All I see on the news are issues about government scandals, partisan blowhards insulting each other, or some military official threatening war with Maxtopia. No wonder our citizens think this country is a disgrace. The government could tone down the craziness and say oh, I don’t know, help out the victims of that earthquake in Blackacre or enact some policies to help end homelessness. Who knows, maybe people will be proud to call themselves Atharvites once again?”

title: Cicadas in Their Prime
text: Hordes of clamoring, noisy and bug-eyed citizens have called upon the government to do something about an expected megaswarm of locusts this coming year.
chosen_option_text: “These fascinating creatures only emerge to swarm at intervals of prime number years, and next year we’re looking at the rare overlap of an 11-year and 19-year cycle,” enthuses Cain Picard, a man with large, weirdly unblinking eyes and a hungry expression. “Sadly though, many wonderful specimens are not going to emerge from the ground because of cementing over of historic breeding habitats! We need to grab some jackhammers, and make The Solutions Guy better for the little guys!”

title: Patently Obvious
text: The popular business simulation game “NationCrates” has been inspiring more Atharvites to start their own companies and develop new products. The backlog of application forms to patent inventions and register trademarks and company names has piled up in patent offices throughout The Solutions Guy, and both civic servants and would-be innovators are laying claims to new devices for banging down your door and making their voices heard.
chosen_option_text: “The registration process should be easier,” complains Hope Wiggum, inventor of the EZ-Fake-Oven, a device that bakes physical versions of Internet cookies. “The future of the economy lies in the people. Self-employment is just the next step we need to take towards bringing that about. In fact, all registration should be done online!”

title: Too Big to Rig
text: Accusations of bid-rigging have arisen after a company run by your brother, Ranil, secured its fourth large government construction contract in a row. After dealing with weeks of complaints from good government advocates — and many impassioned pleas from Ranil to ignore the issue — formal discussion about government contracting has reached your desk.
chosen_option_text: “Why do we bother working with those leeches?” bemoans Ingmar Vega, the head of an obscure maintenance department, who’s currently fixing a pipe in your office. “Why not just have the government do the work directly? It may be expensive to set up, but we won’t have to worry about who’s related to who or ingrates overcharging us, and we’ll create some good-paying jobs in the process. We all know you can always count on the government to deliver high-quality ser—” the pipe then sprays water in his face.

title: A Political Cock-Up
text: A low budget film allegedly showing junior government minister Penny Poindexter in a compromising (though technically legal) position has gone viral on social media. Concerned individuals, especially parents, are loudly voicing their opinions on the matter.
chosen_option_text: “Don’t you think this is taking things a bit far?” queries the minister in question, nervously. “It’s a low-quality video and that could be anyone’s... Okay, it was me. But I don’t do it anymo Okay, I still do it, but it’s biology that made me this way! Can you blame biology? Leader, you can’t deny that I satisfy you with the job I do, so why should it matter how I spend my leisure time?”

title: The End of the Rainbow
text: Art supplies manufacturer VantaSystems recently unveiled their creation of Violent Violet, a pigment far more vivid than any other violet known due to its complex structural properties. Despite the color sparking widespread excitement in the art world, VantaSystems licensed it exclusively to artist Malon Karich, who is refusing to make it available to anyone else.
chosen_option_text: “Karich has the greener position, but let’s go another fence over,” opines T.I. Funny, the eponymous CEO of a major jeweller, spontaneously entering your office after eavesdropping through the door. “Consider colors that are deeply linked with a brand, like the Funny Fuchsia used for our jewelry boxes. This is beyond pigments; without the ability to trademark the color itself no matter how it’s made, all the imitations will put us in the red! Let’s make things a little more black and white: we get to use Funny Fuchsia, and no one else can.”

title: Patent Nonsense
text: After going online for the first time, the National Patent Registration Database (NPRD) has been inundated with countless patent applications, many of them seemingly jokes. One of the worst offenders was the attempted registration of a so-called ‘time machine’, which was simply an alarm clock taped to a microwave. Frustrated patent offices are demanding that you do something to stop these joke proposals.
chosen_option_text: “You must accept all patents regardless of their contents!” demands Sufjan Erso, a self-proclaimed mad scientist, who is submitting his ‘time machine’ application again despite having been rejected at least a dozen times so far. “All inventions have their own merits, and who is to say that something you deem as trash isn’t actually a revolutionary gadget in disguise? The pursuit of science is a worthy cause in itself, and to deny innovators their just reward is an insult to their efforts. Let us and our creations finally be recognised!”

title: Unintelligent Oversight
text: A review of the national budget has revealed that the Atharvite Intelligence Agency has, among other things, been pouring millions of birthday invites into the construction of an “interdimensional time-travelling microwave”. Bewildered at the project, many government officials are accusing the department of wasting their funding.
chosen_option_text: “What a load of hogwash!” exclaims your Minister of Defense, Daveo Cosham, tossing a gelified banana onto your desk. “This is all they have to show for their work! Time travel, multiple dimensions, and super weapons for super soldiers: these are all fine comic book ideas, but utter nonsense for those of us who must live in the real world. It is clear that these ‘intelligence’ agencies have been given far too much freedom to operate. They ought to seek approval from you for all future experimental projects.”

title: The Call of Nature
text: The Solutions Guy has become the laughing stock of the world after The Smalltopian Sentinel published an article on the public urination problem in Risaabussy. This article cited the Smalltopian ambassador, who complained about the sordid stench outside the embassy building. Distraught at the international humiliation, your aides have come to you with a shower of suggestions.
chosen_option_text: “They’re calling us the latrine of The Many States of the Cet!” yells Felicity Benteen, your Minister of Foreign Affairs, holding a violet-scented wet wipe to her nose. “The worst thing is that those despicable Smalltopian tabloids aren’t even wrong: our people are marking their territory on every building wall, and there’s a golden river running alongside every city street. We need to institute punitive fines to deter public urination before our good reputation gets flushed down the toilet!”

title: Rodents of Unusual Sociability
text: Your brother’s pet guinea pig has been looking a little down recently, and a pet psychiatrist has revealed that this is a consequence of loneliness.
chosen_option_text: “If a guinea pig is too miserable, its owner can just dispose of it and get a happier-looking one,” suggests passer-by Lola Bale, tossing a pet cat into a nearby wheeled bin. “Darwinism will take care of the rest, and within a few generations you’ll have a selected population of guinea pigs that doesn’t mind being alone.”

title: Lesson Learnt
text: Statisticians have noted that the prisons of The Solutions Guy are filled disproportionately by the uneducated poor. Many are now debating the advantages of offering education to inmates during their sentences.
chosen_option_text: “Look, lack of formal education doesn’t mean criminals are ignorant, just that they have specialised skills,” observes primary schoolteacher Fumiko vanDyke, handing out ‘You’re Special Too!’ stickers to everyone in the room. “Rather than starting from scratch, why not recognise what skills they have and try to find them suitable work? Murderer? Put that killer instinct to use in the army. Arsonist? Get that knowledge of fire into supervising controlled forest fires. Burglar? Re-purpose those skills in climbing and fine motor control into telephone line repair. It’s all about valuing people for who they actually are.”

title: Outside the Box
text: Heavyweight boxer Chastity Williams faced a lot of criticism when — during a press conference before a title fight — she yelled at her opponent that she was planning to “smash in your skull, bash your brain pan, and send you to the morgue”. This prediction proved to be true, with a punch to the temple fracturing her opponent’s skull, killing her. Now people are asking if the boxer should be held to account for her words and actions.
chosen_option_text: “We all heard the threats, then watched the murder happen!” weeps Nelianneke Dodinas, mother to the deceased boxer. “This was a premeditated act, a killer punch aimed in a way that she knew would be lethal! The law needs to recognise that threats are threats and crime is crime, no matter the sporting context.”

title: Underage Drinkers: Social Menace or Misunderstood?
text: With the advent of alcopops and other cheap liquors marketed at younger drinkers there has been public outcry at the sharp increase in underage drinking.
chosen_option_text: “I never wanted my poor babies to grow up to be alcoholics!” wails Jack Kirk, a parent of three, striding into your office. “And now I’m worried they’ll drink themselves into being no-good slobs before they’ve even grown up! The only way to stop this madness is to really crack down on under-age drinking. Stricter identification laws and severe punishments should do the trick! The present laws are much too soft!”

title: A Shot in the Arm
text: The dreaded Rubellan Measles has made a sudden comeback in The Solutions Guy. The disease, which once killed millions, was thought to be wiped out after a vaccine was discovered fifty years ago. Medical professionals blame a recent anti-vaccination movement, which has turned immunization into a political football.
chosen_option_text: “You know, we wouldn’t have these problems if the population was more scientifically aware,” muses amateur scientist Harriet Roosevelt while pouring a vial of green liquid into a vial of purple liquid. “Movements like these are bred from ignorance and misinformation. If the government took an active role in promoting science and education this problem would go away. You could invest in real scientific studies and programs, make science classes mandatory in schools, and arrest any religious nuts who attempt to disrupt our work. The Solutions Guy would enter a new Golden Age!” The vials of liquid suddenly explode, covering your office with smoke and an unusually colored foam.

title: Being Honest
text: A politician is attempting to have his name legally changed from Harry Butts to Honest Joe Johnson so it will look more appealing on the ballot, but his opponents are crying foul.
chosen_option_text: “Hey, what if we took this a step further?” says Cruella Rodriguez, one of your party’s more creative campaign strategists and successful parliamentarians. “As we’re listing names on the ballot, why don’t we have all our party’s candidates change their middle names just before the election to emphasise our key policies. We can use that space like a miniature campaign poster. Like my name, for example, would be Cruella ‘Quiz Answers Hai Bro?’ Rodriguez. How could people resist voting for that?”

title: Whose Democracy Is It Anyway?
text: After another bill aimed at strengthening youth development activities that was heavily backed by youth organizations was dismissed by the Atharvite legislature for the 65th time this session while unanimously voting to lower the price of oatmeal, outraged youth activists across the nation accuse the increasingly elderly politicians of being out of touch with their concerns.
chosen_option_text: “The adults are not alright!” exclaims teenage ShortTok star and self-proclaimed representative of outraged young people Hope Whitlam. “These blatantly biased votes are what happens when the current legislature consists almost entirely of geriatrics who require round-the-clock nurse aids and afternoon naps. If we only have walking skeletons representing us, how can we trust them to protect the interests of us young people? Bring in age quotas into our government to guarantee that we get an actual say for once!”

title: Fantastic Beasts and How The Solutions Guy Harmed Them
text: A shocking exposé on tourist attraction OceanWorld has revealed the mistreatment of captive orcas and other marine animals. Your office has since faced a tidal wave of complaints demanding government action.
chosen_option_text: “Perhaps there could be a compromise?” queries your Minister of the Environment, Winston Cruise, who has been smelling like grass lately. “Ending zoos would harm the tourism industry, and we can’t deny that these programs help endangered species. Why don’t we set a limit on what animals they take? Specifically the endangered ones? I’m sure that we can also force tougher standards to ensure OceanWorld treats the animals humanely as well.”

title: Lessons in Politics
text: The Politics Department at the University of Narendra Modi City has come under criticism from opposition politicians because the programme is clearly and unashamedly biased in favour of you, Leader, and your political ideologies.
chosen_option_text: “This is not about partisanship; it is about academic autonomy,” retorts Politics Professor Hermione Jackson, signing a copy of her latest book Why Chicago Smells of Fish. “We, as a faculty, just so happen to choose to support your politics. And we just so happen to attract a capable staff who are all like-minded. It is our absolute democratic right to set our own syllabus, without interference from government! You, being one of the wisest leaders that this nation has ever seen, must surely see this!”

title: Ban the ‘Boards, Say Pedestrians
text: The conservative Northern-based parents group of “Housewives and Convicts for a Safer The Solutions Guy” has put forward a memorandum to ban skateboarding in public.
chosen_option_text: “Ticketing children for getting out of the house and exercising?” asks Bianca Mankiller, a school teacher, in disbelief. “That’s outrageous! It’s true that skateboarding can be dangerous but so is walking down the stairs! You want to ban that too?! What we should do is pass laws requiring safety equipment for skaters - if we allocate a little bit of the tax payers’ money to the cause, we can build a skate park that will keep our children safe and away from others on the road too.”

title: Knitters in a Knot Over Police Stitch Up
text: After a peaceful public knitting class was dispersed by riot police, the citizenry are up in arms at what they perceive as unnecessary police brutality.
chosen_option_text: “Retraining the entire police force would cost far too much,” your financial advisor says quietly, appearing from behind your chair. “That being said, the crazy lady with the woolly hat is right, we do have to do something about this situation. We can’t have the police force appear brutal and unruly. What we should do is universally ban all sorts of dangerous weapons. That way the police force won’t have to worry about dangerous thugs with guns, and the public can rest easy knowing the police force won’t be able to brutally attack them either. And we can get rid of the riot police too as they clearly won’t be needed, which saves us money! Everybody wins!”

title: I’ll Have What She’s Having
text: The formerly insignificant nation of Merovingia has come to international attention recently with its patissiers creating a formidable new chocolate cake called “The Grand Moment”. It’s said that this cake has an unusual effect on the biochemistry of women who indulge in it, creating waves of female pleasure that cannot be found elsewhere in the culinary world. Discussions ensue over a family game of Scrabble.
chosen_option_text: “I’m more curious to know about why there’s no male pleasure here,” says your visually-impaired teenage nephew, licking frosting from his fingers. “We should let the women do whatever they like, but let’s spend some research money looking at how to stimulate male neurochemistry. With enough research, I reckon that we could be the world leaders in culinary pleasure for men.”

title: No Representation Without Taxation?
text: The recent publication of a book “Who Pays For Government?”, written by internationally famous economist Millicent Freeman, has triggered a public debate about voting rights.
chosen_option_text: “That’s very stirring rhetoric, but I wonder if everyone really feels that way,” muses libertarian scholar Jenna Wolfeschlegelsteinhausenbergerdorff, a research fellow at the Nyancato Institute. “So why not give everyone the choice? Make it legal for people to sell their votes, and leave it to them to decide what’s more important to them: keeping their vote, or feeding their family.”

title: You Can’t Handle the Tooth
text: A few days ago you needed triple root-canal surgery, and despite your codeine-enhanced prescription you’re still in agony. However, your dentist has refused to prescribe anything stronger! You’re now back for your check-up, wondering if it’s time to think about relaxing the regulations around the most powerful painkillers.
chosen_option_text: “Ummm**HUUURP**..uh, yuck,” says Dental Nurse Moana Fallon, who you know is also a spokesperson for Patients Against Interdicting Narcotics, while emptying a recently-soiled emesis dish into the medical waste sluice. “Yeah, that’s precisely the wrong thing to do. Insufficient treatment of pain is very common, especially among women, ethnic minorities, and the poor. The elderly are also at risk, since many wrongly think that pain is just a ‘normal’ part of aging. The most severe cases can even drive people to suicide! Medicine should focus on quality of life, not just curing disease. Do the right thing, and ease restrictions on powerful painkillers now!”

title: Resting in Peace
text: Truck drivers are complaining that designated highway rest areas are always full, and many have taken to parking by the roadside.
chosen_option_text: “People should buy more local produce instead,” suggests Onya Baike, from the eco-advocate organisation Carbon Counts. “We propose that you should tax cargo-carrying road vehicles increasing amounts proportional to the fuel used in  transportation. I’m sure rising costs create rising prices, which will change consumer behaviour, which will mean less haulage traffic on the road, which means no parking problems.”

title: Suffer Little Children
text: The Durum Pulsaverit Academy — a private educational institution for the offspring of an order of black-clad believers — has caused controversy when it was recently discovered that it was illegally administering corporal punishment on students for a variety of offences, including talking in class and poor penmanship.
chosen_option_text: “Our accusers make it sound like there’s something cruel going on,” intones the school’s headmaster Killsin Barbon, who has a bimonthly lifestyle advice column in the order’s magazine: The Dour Digest. “They see not that it is done in love. A love of inflicting pai... piety. Youth is born wicked — disobedient, full of sin and forever questioning that which it pleases not their superiors to tell them — and such wickedness must be driven out. Our graduates are perfect citizens. Their sin-natures of treason and reason ripped from them, they then go through life as a meek and pure-minded mass. You should bring back corporal punishment in all schools. A beating a day keeps the badness at bay.”

title: Vaping Up a Storm
text: E-cigarettes and vaping have been growing more popular, but some have expressed safety concerns.
chosen_option_text: “Mom, you have like, minus one hundred percent idea what you’re talking about,” retorts her son, fifteen-year-old Faramir, obnoxiously exhaling a cloud of berry-scented vapour into your face. “E-cigarettes have like, no bad stuff in them at all, so they’re as safe to smoke as drinking water. I mean drinking water is as safe as smoking these, not that you can smoke water... uh... you get what I mean. In fact, they help people stop smoking.
