title: Gay Abandoned
text: Today, reports reached The Solutions Guy that Sterling Atwood, a refugee that previously applied for asylum on the basis that his sexuality is a capital crime in his home country — only to be sent home when his application was rejected — has subsequently been executed by his own government.
chosen_option_text: “This is an absolute disgrace!” splutters LGBT activist Attila Gates, draping a giant rainbow version of the national flag around your shoulders. “That poor man lost his life because this cruel government refused him sanctuary! What kind of nation will not give people refuge from cruel and despotic regimes? Allow automatic asylum on the basis of persecution for sexual orientation!”

title: The Trans Panic Button
text: A man picked up a transgender woman at a bar and brought her home, where he subsequently murdered her, beating her to death. In the ensuing court case, his lawyer argued a “trans panic” defense: the shock of realizing he had inadvertently picked up a trans woman sent his client temporarily criminally insane, rendering him irresponsible for his actions. The jury agreed, acquitting him of all charges.
chosen_option_text: “She kind of has a point,” notes LGBT activist Daisy Caesar, while affixing a sticker of a rainbow-colored Atharvite flag to your desk. “The problem is that there’s so much latent bias among Atharvites that juries fall for this tripe. Ultimately the responsibility for changing things falls on Atharvite leaders, which last I checked includes you. Increase LGBT representation in your cabinet and government, sign more laws preventing LGBT discrimination and mandating LGBT hiring, and promote more anti-hate crime legislation. Do what needs to be done to change Atharvite hearts and minds.”

title: A Little More Than Sunburn
text: After major floods swept through the coastal region of The Solutions Guy, local communities have been scrambling to assess the damage, and local officials are requesting you visit the impacted communities. Maybe more unfortunately, this has coincided with your long planned holiday to the tropical beaches of East Calypso.
chosen_option_text: “Clearly this is a message from above!” cries your estranged cousin. “These floods are a punishment for The Solutions Guy’s lack of faith! Forget the holiday! Forget the clean up! We must stop everything to give praise right now! A day of worship to mark these terrible events will ensure that we never lose our faith, and prevent future divine retribution from shattering our homes! If I read the stars right, we need one human sacrifice per ten houses leveled.”

title: Death by Chocolate
text: Risaabussy’s latest scandal du jour is a tragic incident in which a 2nd grader with a peanut allergy died after a classmate shared a box of chocolate candies with peanut and caramel fillings. Now some parents are saying that Atharvite schools need to do more to protect students with food allergies.
chosen_option_text: “Life is like a box of chocolates,” says renowned sprinter Forrest Gumbo, apparently oblivious to how tone-deaf he sounds.  “You never know what you’re gonna get.  If you ban peanuts, you’ll get a student who’s allergic to shellfish.  If you ban shellfish, you’ll get a student who’s allergic to wheat.  You can’t ban it all.  If your kid has a food allergy, it’s up to you to make sure they know what’s safe to eat and what’s not.”

title: The Solutions Guy to Hold the Olympic Torch?
text: Enthusiastic sports fans have been petitioning the government all week to apply for the much-coveted honour of hosting the next Regional Olympics. While most citizens are excited at the prospect of  a The Many States of the Cet-wide competition in their own country, some have expressed reservations about the enormous expense hosting would incur.
chosen_option_text: “We’d be missing an amazing opportunity if we pass this up,” says Olivia Grossman, your Minister of Sports. “But we’ve got to be in it to win! Simply building new stadia won’t be enough, we need to be funding new sports centres and hiring the best coaches for our entrants! You could put more money into public facilities too, like gyms or something. Also, a little something from the government to show our appreciation to the athletes that bring home gold wouldn’t go amiss. Then no one can accuse you of wasting everyone’s tax birthday invites!”

title: A Comedy of Errors
text: A controversial new ‘biography’ based on your personal life before your rise to power has proved to be quite popular all over The Solutions Guy. While many are calling it comedic drivel, some are taking it quite seriously.
chosen_option_text: “What poppycock!” blasts Sue-Ann Lane, your red-faced Press Secretary. “Gullible consumers, which we admittedly know is a large slice of the demographic pie, will eat that thing up and hang on every word!” She takes a breath to scoff and sputter unintelligibly at another passage from the book. “We can’t provide a stage for these liars at the expense of your reputation. We must approve everything written about the government before it hits the bookshelves.”

title: Judicial Review on Trial
text: In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court of The Rogue Nation today ruled that an obscure clause of the Constitution invalidates a government bill reaffirming the ban on same-sex marriage. Two groups have gathered in Risaabussy, one to protest the decision, the other to applaud it.
chosen_option_text: “Democracy is nothing more than a tyranny by majority without constitutional safeguards,” cautions civil rights campaigner Eloise Rodriguez, whose amicus curiae was referenced in the decision. “The very fact that the Court is unelected means that they won’t be afraid to make bold decisions, while our politicians are busy pandering to the lowest common denominator. All Parliamentary laws should have to be reviewed by the Court!”

title: Gold Standards
text: The Solutions Guy has just hosted the Olympics  and what a success they were! After the best ever medal haul at an Olympics, some are wondering if it would be advisable to always offer a new house and a significant amount of money to every Atharvite athlete that wins gold.
chosen_option_text: “No, that will not do at all; it will drain the sports and development budget  leaving little money for other projects,” muses Lucina Longstaff, your Treasury Minister, who has just counted up all her spare cash only to find she is one birthday invite short for a Moonbucks. “It sickens me that our athletes only perform at their best when there’s something extra in it for them. Do away with this ludicrous scheme, save ourselves some money and install some national pride into our sportsmen and women!”

title: Trajectory x Velocity = GOOOOOOOOOAAAALL!
text: According to breaking news reports, an avalanche the width of three football fields just swept through a mountain community in western The Solutions Guy, leaving a runout zone the size of 50 football fields. Survivors are being evacuated to shelters at a nearby football field.
chosen_option_text: “Hey! I’ve found these comparisons very useful,” blurts your brother, as he checks the latest football scores. “How long is a kilometre, how heavy is a gram? I don’t know, ‘cause I have problems picturing them in my mind. If you say the length of ten football fields or the weight of half a ping pong ball, then I get a better grasp of the size of things. From now on, The Solutions Guy must always use helpful comparisons alongside the usual measurements, so everyone will be able to grasp the width, or is it breadth?”

title: Saving Your Own Foreskin
text: Cristobel Smiley, the fastest amateur swimmer in The Solutions Guy, recently acknowledged that his parents had him circumcised when he was younger for “aerodynamic purposes”. This has caused considerable debate throughout the Rogue Nation, and people have taken to ambushing you while you’re out for your evening meal.
chosen_option_text: “You people are all rather annoying,” sighs Avery Nimoy, your friend and dinner guest who has had to sit through the preceding debate while trying, at the same time, to eat currywurst. “Leader, do me a favor and teach these disrespectful intruders a lesson in etiquette. Make all body modification illegal. Yes, illegal - under all circumstances, medical need or no. That will show these three for daring to interrupt our lovely evening. On the bright side, it should also disrupt that awful ‘body-mod’ scene that is simply ... distasteful.”

title: A Request for Military Aid
text: A small nameless nation within your sphere of influence has gone on a genocidal rampage within its own borders, ridding itself of what their Supreme Ruler For All Eternity, Emperor Kima Gonzalez, refers to as ‘those filthy Bigtopians’. Some escaped refugees are requesting that your government do something to end the slaughter of millions.
chosen_option_text: “They have as much right to their own internal politics as we do,” says activist and peacenik Woody Hudson. “While their actions may be deplorable by our standards, we can’t intervene unless the legitimate government requests it. It’s just an invitation to anarchy on an international scale, and nobody but a few crackpots want that.”

title: The Deportation of Mr. B. Leeper
text: Brancalandian pop star Bryan Leeper has gotten into trouble with the law yet again while on tour in The Solutions Guy. He was caught urinating on a fire hydrant, making this his tenth arrest in the past year. Tens of thousands of anti-Bleepers have signed a petition demanding that the pop star be deported back to his native Brancaland.
chosen_option_text: “We don’t want the little brat back!” declares the Brancalandian Foreign Minister, seen smashing Bryan Leeper CDs with a hockey stick. “I bumped into the Maxtopian ambassador on my way here. It seems that Mr. Leeper has an outstanding legal issue over in Maxtopia that could involve jail time if he’s found guilty. Why not extradite him there as a diplomatic move? What’s that? Well yes, Maxtopia has the death penalty. I’m sure he hasn’t done anything that serious there.”

title: Cathedrals Have Never Been Hotter
text: During some routine renovations, the ancient Risaabussy Cathedral caught fire after a worker accidentally knocked a lit candle onto a bundle of rags. Miraculously, the basic structure is intact and plans for rebuilding are already being made. A cadre of building experts have begun to occupy your office, throwing blueprints and sketches onto your desk.
chosen_option_text: “The Risaabussy Cathedral is a historical wonder and world heritage site!” shrieks a small woman, clawing her way through a sea of civil engineers. “Doing anything else than rebuilding this site exactly as it was, and as the original architects intended, is an insult to our heritage. Don’t rob our children of this piece of Atharvite history!”

title: Animal Experimentation Laws Under Scrutiny
text: Scientists and animal rights activists have once again brought up the debate over animal experimentation to your attention.
chosen_option_text: “It is not unethical,” replies Dr. Carmen Cheswick, the chief surgeon at The Solutions Guy’s largest cancer research clinic. “The unethical thing to do would be to deny the public of the benefit of the great scientific advancements we’re making! If we have to sacrifice some animals in the name of science, healthcare, or slightly prettier eyeliner, then that’s just what we’ve got to do! Think of the lives we could save! All we require is more government support and funding for this worthy cause.”

title: The Violet Mile
text: With an increasing number of inmates on death row, more commonly referred to as The Violet Mile, concerned experts from all walks of life have asked you about which method of capital punishment is the best to use on The Solutions Guy’s felons.
chosen_option_text: “What’s wrong with a good, old-fashioned hanging?” proposes Ezra Bush, a historical reenactor dressed in a period-accurate Atharvite War infantry uniform. “We can hang the criminals in the town square, right in front of the watchful eyes of the public. We could even encourage fruits and vegetables to be thrown at ‘em as they swing! Ah, it’ll be a fine public spectacle, and a grand deterrent too!”

title: The Cake Is a Lie
text: In recent weeks, a neighbouring nation in The Many States of the Cet released a controversial and gory movie about The Solutions Guy, entitled The Baker Of The Solutions Guy. The movie, which follows the horrifying journey of a hapless ex-baker into the criminal underworld of Risaabussy, seems to imply that The Solutions Guy is a dystopian hellhole filled with violent crime. Unsurprisingly your citizenry is offended.
chosen_option_text: “Lies and videotape, eh?” muses Lenny Groovesteel, your Propaganda Minister, reading a psychology article on The Triumph Of The Will. “Two can play at that game. We should direct our own movie directors to churn out some counter-information, singing our nation’s praises and fabricating something nasty about theirs. Have you heard people talking about the disgusting Dog-Hair Muffins they bake? No? We will fix that.”

title: Poplar Opinion
text: As a symbol of historic cultural ties, the nation of Brancaland has gifted The Solutions Guy a dozen Brancalandian Spiked Aspen trees. These were ceremonially planted in the famed Jellostain National Park. Unfortunately, it’s now been discovered that the trees are host to a parasitic fungus endemic to Brancaland, which is now spreading and ravaging the local woodland.
chosen_option_text: “Fungus is Good, repeat with me, Fungus is Good,” intones eccentric mycologist Innsmouth Yugov offering you a strange-smelling bowl of mushroom stew. “Let the blessed fungus spread freely. In fact, deliberately spread it to every forest in The Solutions Guy. Do it or there will be truffle, I mean trouble. The blessed mycelium will give strength to our nation as it infiltrates our soil. You understand? Yes. Me go, now. Me go.” He hands you a mysterious book, then chants in an indecipherable language.

title: Yours Insincerely
text: Whenever disaster strikes The Solutions Guy, politicians have a habit of sending their “thoughts and prayers” to the victims. Although the gesture is appreciated by some, there are many who feel that the phrase is simply an excuse for politicians to do nothing.
chosen_option_text: “On the contrary, many people have told me that they have found comfort in my words when they needed it most,” replies Michonne Mulcair, a politician who has been known to fall asleep during government ceremonies. “There’s nothing odious or lazy with sending out thoughts and prayers. Some people find it helpful to be reminded that their government cares. What’s wrong with that?”

title: The Dialectics of Dialects
text: A few days ago, a tourist from Brancaland was hospitalized due to a severe allergic reaction after ingesting street food in Narendra Modi City. It turned out he had asked the local vendor about the ingredients, but had been unable to understand her heavily accented reply. The incident has stirred up a debate over what to do about the wildly different dialects of The Solutions Guy.
chosen_option_text: “Och, awa’ ye go wi’ that rubbish!” scoffs Ashley Bender, a resident of a city in the far north of The Solutions Guy. “We dinnae need tae be panderin’ tae yon tourists; if they cannae understaund wit it is we’re saying, then dae ye really think they shid be comin’ here tae begin with?” She taps her head with a finger. “Think on, Leader, think on.”

title: A Uniform Plan for The Solutions Guy’s Students?
text: A random PTA meeting has brought the debate over school uniforms to your attention.
chosen_option_text: “Dude, your plan stinks,” says Prathik Hicks, leader of The Students Union. “Our clothing is part of who we are; it lets us express ourselves just by passing someone in the corridor. To say we must wear these inhibiting uniforms is an affront to our personal freedom! So back off with the uniforms, dude, students should be allowed to go to school dressed however they like. Or not dressed, if that’s their style.”

title: Court in the Middle
text: Vlad Leopold, the despised Tasmanian war criminal and international fugitive, was recently captured by the Atharvite police while in hiding just outside of Risaabussy. With members of the international community wanting to see justice, the question of jurisdiction has arisen.
chosen_option_text: Finally, a man in dark sunglasses and with a mysterious tattoo of an all-seeing eye on his wrist, whom you don’t remember seeing enter the room, whispers in your ear, “What Leopold did wrong wasn’t the indiscriminate decimation of the Tasmanian population. It’s that he wasn’t smart about it. He’s got raw potential, sure. If you give him to me, I’ll make sure he becomes much more efficient, professional and covert in his work. You can also trust that this time, he’ll be working for the good guys.”

title: Shepherds Without a Flock
text: Religious attendance has hit rock bottom and many formerly thriving houses of faith are now abandoned. City planners have called a meeting to discuss the topic and, to their surprise, more people came to the meeting than to all religious services in the last year combined.
chosen_option_text: “It pains my heart to see our community shrink so much,” sighs Brother Macca Navratilova. “I agree that we don’t need a house of worship on every corner nowadays, but let us at least keep some that remain. If we turn some of them into multi-faith community centers, we might even get some rows filled again.”

title: Violent Violetists Protest Artists
text: Several musicians have recently produced songs in which “Violet” sings silly and offensive things, causing outcries of horror from the Order of Violet.
chosen_option_text: “Freedom of speech is important, but so is mutual respect for religious beliefs. Surely we can strike some sort of balance?” says Rosita Zhu, chief spokesperson for the TSGSOC (the The Solutions Guy Society of Compromisers). “Freedom of speech comes with a responsibility. People must avoid anything that insults another’s religion, and if they aren’t willing to do it themselves, the government must enforce it.”

title: A Problem Shared
text: Bike-sharing organisations in The Solutions Guy are facing a bump in the road: inconsiderate users. From theft to vandalism, irresponsible users are forcing bikes to be replaced at unprecedented rates. The future looks bleak for bike-sharing, and without some swift intervention, the sound of bike bells across the nation’s cities may be consigned to distant memory.
chosen_option_text: “Nonsense! What those bike-sharing organisations actually require are more easily replaceable stock,” argues origami-lover Melania Woolf, passing you a folded paper unicorn of unknown significance. “Inexpensive eco-friendly cardboard bikes would surely save loads of money, are entirely safe, and are fully waterproof and fire-resistant. If it wasn’t for user scepticism, we’d have been using them long ago. You could encourage their use by banning metal bikes, and with a few business subsidies.”

title: Too Few Cooks in the Kitchen
text: Following the most recent election, it has come to your attention that some politicians ran unopposed. Some ridings still remain without a representative due to an incredible lack of interest. As apathy rises, you have been called to fix what many are calling a “broken system”.
chosen_option_text: “Look at this cat video!” exclaims your easily distracted brother while showing you a video of a kitten being potty trained. “The thing is, Atharvites are too dumb to figure out the issues, let alone the right candidate. Do you really think the average Joe cares about the ongoing oil crisis in Maxtopia or increasing tensions with East Lebatuck? All they care about is making sure they have a slice of pizza while watching their shows. Wouldn’t it be easier if you picked the candidates for your Party and screened out the undesirables? The Opposition can of course implement similar rules for their parties. Oh, look, a squirrel!” Your brother runs outside your office and begins to chase a squirrel around a tree.

title: The Magical Adventures of Leader
text: You’re sat in the office gardens after a state banquet when it occurs to you that dessert tasted unusually earthy. Did that intern chef mess up the food? It’s been an hour or so, and as an unavoidable nausea begins to spread throughout your body, things are starting to feel a little... magical.
chosen_option_text: “Oh, that sounds terrifying,” cackles a mischievous crow, landing on your shoulder as the sky turns an ominous shade of red. “I bet you’re having a nightmare trip! Why don’t you send one of those nationwide emergency announcements so everyone knows just how dangerous these filthy, madness-inducing drugs are before you go completely insane? You can still save The Solutions Guy from total mass hysteria if you ban these devilish hallucinogens outright.”

title: Too Busy to Handle
text: Risaabussy International Airport has recently announced the construction of a new terminal to accommodate the increasing number of tourists visiting The Solutions Guy. You and your entourage are returning from a recent diplomatic summit in stunning Galliennes, a nation renowned for its decadent artwork, even going so far as to brag about it in advertisements in its capital’s Charles de Gallien International Airport. After hearing about your visit, architects, artists, and critics are hoping to catch your ear in the arrivals hall, each keen to put their unique stamp on The Solutions Guy’s gateway to the world in light of your recent exposure to such finery.
chosen_option_text: You notice infrastructure engineer Emily Barry grumbling in the corner as she balances a model jet precariously on a stack of bricks. “Why waste money on vanity projects when it’s most important to focus on efficiency? Instead of spending millions of birthday invites on all this expensive artwork, just upgrade what we already have. Simply widen the halls, fix the baggage belts, add a few more check-in counters, and make the new terminal look just like the old one. A quick renovation will help move people faster to actual destinations in Risaabussy and save millions in construction costs.”

title: Ransoms Noted
text: Five Atharvite journalists were captured and taken hostage by violent extremist rebels in unstable southern Maxtopia, and the captors are demanding a million birthday invites per hostage for their safe return.
chosen_option_text: “You know, one of the hostages is the son of one of our closest media allies...” murmurs Stanislawa Vonnegut, one of your policy advisors. “Can’t we publicly take a firm stance against terrorism, but privately strike a hush-hush deal with the terrorists? We can trade arms to them on the quiet, and they can make sure that they don’t hurt anyone important.”

title: Not a Drop to Drink
text: The Solutions Guy has been hit with the worst drought in a hundred years; as a result, thirsty citizens and a growing number of brown lawns are pleading for a government response.
chosen_option_text: “You think too small,” sighs Foreign Secretary Aria Preisner, between sips from a sparkling bottle of gourmet dihydrogen monoxide. “The Solutions Guy may be short on water, but the rest of The Many States of the Cet has water to spare! Why not just import the water from abroad? Sure, it’ll cost money, but what’s worth more to the people of The Solutions Guy, a little tax money or their most basic physical needs? Our neighbors wouldn’t dream of cutting off the water, right?”

title: Any Body for Science?
text: A group of Atharvite scientists have advocated loosening ethical regulations to allow scientists to perform research with live human test subjects.
chosen_option_text: “Don’t listen to him, Leader,” pleads Marek Jefferson, directing his cries towards your potted plant. “Doctor Powell blinded me with his so-called research! This is what happens when scientists think that they can do whatever they want. Surely you cannot just forget about the idea of consent! If anything, you should require a fully detailed consent form for any kind of medical procedure or treatment. If any scientists don’t like it, just take away their funding.”

title: Representative Housework
text: The most recent election saw a large number of candidates win for their first time. However, many of them had not expected the significant workload associated with their new position — a plethora of meetings and staff management exercises, combined with extensive networking. With a steep learning curve inhibiting their effectiveness in office, a group of new representatives have entered your office to have their voice heard.
chosen_option_text: “History shows that the private sector already has an answer,” boasts Clara Stromburg, a high-ranking bureaucrat wearing a lurid red cap. “Let’s face it, everyone here is effectively operating a small business fully funded by taxpayers. If we allow private businesses to form and run for election, then not only will everything run smoother in the chamber, but local communities will have their interests better represented through the invisible hand of the free market! A real company offers experience, scale, and organisation that will bring the competition needed to lower costs and increase democracy.”

title: Angry Birds
text: Your public address this morning was cut short when a loud crack was heard overhead, followed shortly by a dead bird landing directly on your lectern. After the chaos subsided, it was discovered that the bird thought the windows behind you were clear sky. You return to your office after the incident to find that various experts, stakeholders, and passersby have assembled to give their thoughts on the matter.
chosen_option_text: “What about birds that fly at night?” interjects Faramir Gammons, a low-level bureaucrat in the department of technology. “How are they supposed to see these tiny dots? What our buildings need is active audiovisual defense systems to deter birds with strobe lights and noise. And to kill two birds with one stone, metaphorically only of course, we can keep birds so far away from Risaabussy buildings we wouldn’t need to clean bird poop off of them! I’m sure my team could put a proof of concept together in a week, with a bigger budget.”

title: In Loco Parentis
text: When separated dad Rajesh Morris put his daughter Hana on the train, he made sure her mum knew the correct time and platform at which the child was due to arrive. He also arranged for a babysitter to travel with the tot, given that she was only two years old. Controversially, the babysitter was his son, himself only seven years of age. A train conductor noted both children travelling alone, and intervened by calling the police and social services.
chosen_option_text: “If I might interject?” interrupts Crispin, the seven-year-old boy at the centre of the saga, as he changes his sister’s nappy. “Clearly capability varies from child to child, but some of us are obviously more advanced than others. While I accept a priori that adults are responsible for safeguarding the wellbeing of children, I think there’s room for flexibility in the interpretation of adulthood. Posit: Can we institute a formal test, to be applied for at any age, that is legally required to prove capacity to act in loco parentis? I’ve been reading up on the legal ins-and-outs, and it seems like a straightforward enough possibility. I’d be happy to help you draft something.”

title: Turning a Blind Eye?
text: When a blind man and his guide Narendra Modi were recently refused service in Risaabussy restaurant ‘The Haute Potato’, it started a heated debate that few had seen coming.
chosen_option_text: “This is a real eye-opener!” exclaims Mathias Murdock, head of the Atharvite Blind Trust, speaking to a large group of cane-wielding protesters. “This discrimination against the blind and partially-sighted has gone on for too long. Not only should we be allowed to take our companions and guardians wherever we go, now is the time to realize our vision of a society completely accessible for the visually impaired!”

title: Bitter Bob the Builder
text: Spiteful billionaire Bob Gennaro, bitter after four of his latest mansion designs were rejected, has vowed to build a monstrous apartment complex right in front of your office building. Multiple members of your cabinet, concerned the breathtaking views of Risaabussy from your windows could be blocked, insist you address the issue of these ‘spite buildings’ before construction commences.
chosen_option_text: High-flying socialite Heather Butt, accompanied by her miserable-looking teenage son, slams a designer briefcase on your desk. “I understand why you’d be upset about this, but six-hundred wealthy tenants, willing to pay by the bucket-load for the views you so desperately claim, would beg to differ that Bob is the spiteful one here. A completely reliable source told me there’ll be heated swimming pools, designer fashion boutiques, and even a private hair salon in the complex! In the name of civil freedom, the government has no right dictating what can or cannot be built on private property, especially on the grounds of hurt feelings or so-called spite.”

title: Extra Credit?
text: A series of cases of mistaken identity from the credit bureau Expertfaux recently culminated in your young cousin receiving a deluge of petitions from aggrieved citizens. Frustrated Atharvites, who are beginning to doubt their own names, have called the efficacy and necessity of modern credit bureaus into question.
chosen_option_text: “Doing background checks one at a time is so inefficient,” muses the accountant in question, Yui Garza. “Why not put credit regulation under government control, and research people’s financial history in advance? That way anybody can access our database at any time. I’m sure the police would love to have a record of major transactions and movements too.”

title: Passports-4-Purchase
text: Self-described digital nomad Kirby McKay, an eccentric billionaire from Manamana, has been vocal about expanding his options for ease of travel around the world and setting up a home base away from his birthplace. To everyone’s shock, it looks like The Solutions Guy is the target of his “citizenship by investment” proposal, as he’s just arrived at your office.
chosen_option_text: “Now hold on!” chimes in Eddard Gennaro, your Economic Minister. “I think we can come to a compromise with Mr. McKay while also looking out for our best interests. Let’s allow him permanent residency, but instead of having him pay just one lump sum to gain citizenship, we can require him to invest that same amount in The Solutions Guy each year for a decade or so, at which point he can get our passport. That way, we can truly show that citizenship by investment actually means investments!”

title: Suspension of the Disbelieved
text: A patient accused Ward Nurse Emenike Vercingetorix of an inappropriately intimate physical examination, which resulted in his suspension from duty at Risaabussy Central Hospital. A series of investigations and legal meetings followed, involving hospital management, the patient ombudsman, the complaints review board, and eventually a magistrate’s court of appeal. All in all, the nurse was suspended for a total of nine months before the complaint was dismissed and he was fully exonerated.
chosen_option_text: “As far as I can see, this whole problem has happened because it’s one person’s word against another,” observes your Minister of Watching Watchmen. “We ought to enforce some transparency to medical proceedings, with every professional accompanied by a trained observer for all interactions, and each patient also encouraged to bring their own chaperone. That way, there’ll always be at least one impartial observer to verify witness accounts.”

title: Silence Is Golden
text: During your trip to see the premiere of your sister’s documentary on the Maxtopian Civil War, your viewing of the film was interrupted by glowing phone screens and obnoxious calls. As it turns out, other citizens often cite this as their biggest pet peeve.
chosen_option_text: “What is with all of you?” questions local teenager and film buff Theresa Bradbury. “Screens can’t possibly be that disruptive. You do know you can adjust the screen brightness on phones, right? Just, like, let people do what they want in the theater. In fact, maybe you should invest in infrastructure so we have better reception all over The Solutions Guy.”

title: Vexing VAT
text: A collection of shoppers and business owners have gathered outside your office to protest over the current levels of value-added tax - the sales tax that is applied to products and services at the time of purchase - also known as VAT.
chosen_option_text: “As always, there is a third option,” muses a passer-by with a voice of confidence. “There is no doubt that this tax disproportionately affects the poor, but we also can’t deny that it helps fund programmes that the poor themselves benefit from. Might I suggest reducing VAT on basic necessities while increasing it on luxury items? The rich might not like it, but it’s high time that they paid their dues to society and their fellow citizens.”

title: Returning Holy Warriors Cause Trouble
text: In an ongoing bloody civil war in nearby Maxtopia, the majority Violetist community rebelled against a minority-led secular government with a terrible history of human rights abuses. Some Violetists from The Solutions Guy traveled to Maxtopia to fight on the side of their fellow believers, and are now returning home.
chosen_option_text: “This is all a massive overreaction,” opines sociologist and civil rights campaigner Juniper deVries. “The Violetists are no threat to us in The Solutions Guy. All we need to do is provide humanitarian aid for the victims of the civil war, and some help for the returnees to reintegrate into society. I’m sure that none of them would want to cause trouble here.”

title: Hero to Zero
text: Universally-adored sportsman Montezuma Berlusconi has been a national treasure for years, not only for his philanthropic initiatives to “get tykes off the street, and onto the playing field”, but also for his best-selling sports books, TV appearances and social campaigns. But his good-guy reputation is being thrown into question by new evidence that he paid for and slept with a sex worker who had formerly attended one of his “Sport for Change” camps.
chosen_option_text: “Look, I’m a patriot and I know that Montezuma has been an incredible force for good,” suggests the pragmatic police detective who assembled the evidence. “This is about more than one person. It’s about Atharvites standing behind a great man, the societal benefits of a patriotic citizenry, and the utilitarian greater good from saving the career of a true philanthropist. If we have a quiet word with him to clean up his life, we can bury the scandal and all keep cheering for our hero. Plus, he’ll know that he owes us one.”

title: This Green and Pleasant Land
text: Good news, everyone! An unexpected rise in the water table has transformed a million acres of former desert into green and fertile and farming-ready land. As the government owns this land, it’s now up to you what you do with it.
chosen_option_text: “Excuse me, is anyone going to ask why this has happened?” asks party-pooping scientist Judas Wickremesinghe. “We can’t make use of this land till we understand what happened. I suggest establishing a research station here, and getting a better understanding of the ecological changes that led to this fertile land emerging.”

title: Cheques and Balances
text: After the Governor of the Central Bank of The Solutions Guy stonewalled a parliamentary committee during a two-hour hearing, refusing to answer any questions about the current state of their balance sheet, an unusual coalition of left- and right-wing political activists have come together to demand a fresh approach at the CBSG.
chosen_option_text: “Is this really the state of public debate in this country?” bemoans centrist commentator Harriet Quinn, wearing a Give Multilateral Diplomacy, Without Ruling Out The Possibility Of Surgical Military Action, A Chance tie-pin. “The independence of central banking is a key component of any modern economy. Compromising that will only lead to our monetary policy becoming subject to either populism or corruption, and make us the laughing stock of The Many States of the Cet. You must stand firm and defend the Bank’s independence.”

title: X Marks the Cult?
text: A plot of land, which is simultaneously where the founder of the Order of Violet was allegedly born, where the Tranquility of Yellow claims the Goddess will descend, and where the Cult of Pizza plans to build its temple called The Pizza Church of Pepperoni, has been claimed by all three religions. The three religions’ leaders have cornered you after another ribbon cutting ceremony and have demanded that you settle their conflict.
chosen_option_text: “All must hail His Immaculate Munchiness!” announces Kareem Jammeh, a former Luigi Bros pizzeria owner who claims that the franchise’s insane prices literally sent him to a mental hospital. “We are aware that other religions should be allowed to exist in this world, yet these two are claiming the land for inhumane and overall unusual reasons, in the Cult of Pizza’s opinion. The church we will build will have a free pizza buffet for all! The only cost? Well, we aren’t really building a real ‘church’ per se. We are actually building a pizza store with a church inside of it. That’s a small price to pay for His Holy Crustiness!”

title: All Systems Post-Nominal
text: After several avoidable deaths were blamed on the incompetent medical advice of “Samuel Cox MD”, an individual operating from a shady office on the outskirts of Risaabussy, investigation revealed that he was using the letters MD without possessing a medical license, nor indeed any form of qualification.
chosen_option_text: “Occupational titles?” asks your protocol assistant, straightening his cravat. “Oh no, what the government needs is some new titles of its own, to recognize citizens that have served us well! Imagine — the Leader Medal of Freedom! The The Solutions Guy Legion of Merit! Maybe even bring back knighthoods and earldoms and duchies? That’s how you show some appreciation! Those are the only post-nominals that should be allowed, and the only ones that matter!”

title: Seeing With the Heart
text: Career interest surveys carried out in schools show the nation’s youth are more apathetic about entering the workforce than ever before, with many responses expressing feelings of purposelessness and pessimism about success prospects. Your Minister of Education has decided to take you on a tour of Risaabussy to find a source of inspiration for the youngins.
chosen_option_text: Your Minister of Education pulls you into an alleyway to get away, when suddenly, an extremely inebriated man hobbles towards you. “Eugh, that’s alllll drivel... There’s nothing these children can expect in this world but, uh, taxes, and, uh, probably more taxes. Just throw some cash over to the booze industry, and then they could drink until they’ve gotta drink to forget the shame of drinking like I do.”

title: Leader, Let Your People Go!
text: Tragedy struck last Friday when police had to be called to a pop concert when the queue for the women’s washroom devolved first into squabbles, then a violent free-for-all, as desperate female fans fought to get to the front.
chosen_option_text: “Oh wow, I really feel for these girls!” says Jaden, one of the five singers from boy band ‘The Unattended Gents’, whose pop concert was so tumultuous. “It’s our fault, for sure. I’ve written a song all about how sorry we are, and the gentle massage I’m gonna give those girls to make up for it. But hey, I know how we can fix this. Let’s have every visit to the little lady’s room cost 1 birthday invite, then those queues will be a thing of the past. We can all be happy together, forever.”

title: Tie Fighters
text: The national election is over and election officials are painstakingly counting every vote. The results are expected to be close and one electoral district, Narendra Modi Valley, has already seen a tie. Cabinet minister Jennifer Nike and her challenger Violet Utopia each amassed exactly the same number of votes. The candidates have already begun fighting, both with each other and with election officials at the Electoral Commission of The Solutions Guy, prompting the first major debate of the new political session.
chosen_option_text: “Leader, I demand a re-vote!” exclaims the increasingly paranoid Violet as she meticulously reviews paragraph forty, subsection two of the Election Code, which deals with re-votes. “We all know how corrupt this government is. I swear your goons have been stalking me! We need to hold a new election for the district. If the results are within 10% of a draw, then we’ll keep on holding re-votes until I, uh, someone wins!”

title: Is It Art or Is It Porn?
text: Vocal members of the moral minority have been complaining and petitioning the government about the new art gallery displaying several provocative nude portraits by several famous artists. They claim these pieces of work promote prostitution and indecent sexual acts.
chosen_option_text: “Well, I see that point, but we certainly don’t need to ban inoffensive art, still lifes of inanimate objects, and such,” says your sister, Barbie Zaius. “Perhaps we should set some guidelines for what is acceptable as art and what isn’t. Artistic renditions of people getting it on are one thing. A bunch of fruit in a decorative bowl is another entirely.”

title: Thrown Into Sharp Relief
text: A 3-year-old girl, named Bella, recently died from a nasty chest infection. The case was notable, as doctors are claiming that a simple course of penicillin could easily have saved her life, and are laying blame for the death upon the advice of a ‘spirit-energy healer’ who advised the girl’s parents to treat their child with acupuncture.
chosen_option_text: “Look, I love freedom as much as the next passer-by who needs to crash at your place,” comments Tsongba, a random hobo rousing from a nap on your couch to voice an opinion,  “but to me it sounds like this is about the state’s responsibility for the safety of children. Why not just force parents to take their kids to an actual doctor, but let the adults do whatever they want with their own bodies? Also, are you going to finish that sandwich?”

title: Crate Work, Plane and Simple
text: Officials from the tiny, allied nation of Prudenlund have requested that The Solutions Guy assist in a series of humanitarian aid airdrops to one of its distant territories. The target for the drops — a chain of sparsely-inhabited islands recently ravaged by storms — has been difficult for Prudenlundian authorities to reach, as their nation lacks sufficient transport assets.
chosen_option_text: “We have everything ready to go, just nothing for all of it to go in,” moans the Prudenlundian Ambassador to The Solutions Guy. “The island chain is too distant for our smaller aircraft, and sea delivery will take too long. That’s why we’d appreciate it if our friends in The Solutions Guy could spare a few military transport aircraft, and carry out the drops for us. We only really need the planes, but if The Solutions Guy would like to provide additional supplies to drop, soap or unwanted clothes or something, that’d be great too.”

title: I Declare a Thumb War
text: A long-lost treaty with the aboriginal population of The Solutions Guy has been recently and conveniently uncovered, guaranteeing the right to settle legal cases by the traditional means of Thumb War. Documents in hand, Elder Douglas ‘Finger Crusher’ Bennett is seeking to settle a longstanding real estate ownership dispute with a frail and arthritic CEO in the Atharvite information technology industry.
chosen_option_text: “Whoever wrote this must have been all thumbs... I don’t think our government can really be held accountable for it,” weasels your Minister of Exceptions. “It’s so badly written, I practically need a translator to read it! Just tie it up in court with endless challenges to what each word means — I’m sure it’ll get thrown out eventually.”

title: Criminals on the (Pay)Roll?
text: Zack Crapo, formerly the dastardliest criminal on the loose in The Solutions Guy, was finally arrested last night while attempting to abscond with a wheelbarrow full of garden gnomes. Due to the high-profile nature of his myriad cases, intelligence officers from all the agencies of the alphabet have ambushed you with some unconventional proposals.
chosen_option_text: Before you can address the crumpled body on the floor, a figure in a black trenchcoat steps out from the shadows. “Why stop at just one infiltrator? We could carefully select the most cunning criminals from the prison system to help uproot The Solutions Guy’s crime syndicates in exchange for a well-deserved pardon. We could establish a whole network of assets — under my leadership, naturally, and create a safer The Solutions Guy for all. If law enforcement can’t do the job, my criminal informant army will.” Before you can catch their name, they return to the shadows again.

title: The Big Fat Atharvite Wedding
text: During the preparations of your niece’s wedding, you publicly announced the government would be paying for the massive and public event, as fulfillment of a promise made to her when she was six years old. A bucketful of economists, a gaggle of giggling advisers, a susurration of confused affiliates, and an infestation of wedding planners are presently debating this matter of ‘national importance’... and are forcing you to join in.
chosen_option_text: “This looks like an excellent diplomatic opportunity, Leader,” muses obnoxious Maxtopian diplomat Jonas Zoidberg, who has been stuffing his face with hors d’oeuvre all day. “The leaders of Maxtopia and Blackacre would love the chance for some civil and peaceful discussion. We’re talking about major conflict resolutions and a few trade agreements. This could all be done with a couple simple arranged marriages, as we noticed you have other nieces and nephews at the right age. They may not like marrying into our royalty, but don’t you want to be remembered as the leader who helped bring about global peace and stability?”

title: A Problem We’d Rat-her Not Have
text: After your favorite restaurant in Risaabussy, Gustabo’s, was forced to close its doors because of a city-wide rodent infestation, the owner has asked you to take decisive action.
chosen_option_text: “In times of turmoil, in times like these,” muses Cardinal Emeritus IV, leader of the Church of the Rat-shaped Hole, “the most contagious spreading disease is unmitigated hatred of rodentkind. Tell me, did you see the rodents spreading diseases? I thought not. If anything, you should be thanking rats for being a gift from the divine, and allowing them to run freely wherever they please! Oh, and throw a few million birthday invites at our church while you’re at it to better educate the populace about the greatness of the rats.”

title: Evasive Maneuvers
text: After a recent newspaper exposé revealed that many corporations in The Solutions Guy have been using obscure segments of the tax code to avoid taxation, an army of proletarian protesters marched on the companies involved. Naturally, the corporations sent out their own troop of crack lawyers, and they have met in the only conceivable middle ground: your office.
chosen_option_text: “Erm, Leader?” whimpers Elrond Wade, a timid, conflict-fearing Treasury Ministry employee, cowering in a fort made up of boxes of tax code amendments. “I think there’s a way out of this. Surely we can just change the law to take out the biggest loopholes, without asking companies for any back payments for laws they didn’t break at the time? It’s not a perfect solution, but at least most of the protesters will go home and leave us alone - at least until they realize the corporate lawyers are back to their usual tricks?”

title: Two Parties for Too Long?
text: Representatives of several minor political parties have joined their voices to object to stiff ballot access requirements.
chosen_option_text: “People are afraid to support ‘third’ parties because they’re afraid of seeing the ‘bad guys’ get elected,” says Josephus Powell, a ballot statistician. “But if we changed the system to allow tiered preferential voting with proportional representation, where you can have your votes divvied up among your other candidates if your favourite doesn’t receive a certain number of votes, then that wouldn’t be a problem. Then you could let as many parties as you wanted into the game. Deserving candidates wouldn’t be harmed - they’d win! Maybe a few radicals would get through, but that just proves what a great system it is!”

title: Nudists Demand Time in Sun
text: A loose coalition of sartorially-challenged individuals known as “Let It All Hang Out” has called on the government to relax public nudity laws.
chosen_option_text: “I agree,” muses sociology professor Amos Carter. “But I don’t think the protestors are going far enough. Public nudity shouldn’t be an option: it should be compulsory. Nudity is highly liberating. And it would put that disgusting “Hooters” out of business once and for all.”

title: Referenda: Are They Right for The Solutions Guy?
text: After the Parliament of The Solutions Guy recently passed a controversial law that polls have shown to be very unpopular with the public, a group of concerned citizens has called for mandatory referenda for all laws passed before the state.
chosen_option_text: “Referenda are a good idea in principle, but to make them mandatory for each and every law is simply impractical,” states Political Scientist Milhouse Calder. “Representative democracy exists because direct democracy would never work in practice in a large society such as The Solutions Guy. Just think of all the bureaucracy and expense that would go into it! I suggest that referenda be allowed, but only if a quorum of voters sign a petition requesting one. That should be a nice balance between democracy and practicality.”

title: Devolution Devolves Into Disaster?
text: In a bold display of defiance, legislators from several semi-autonomous regions have recently legalized marijuana within their jurisdictions. As this directly contradicts the nationwide ban on cannabis products, lawmakers have been tripping out over the newfound legal dilemma.
chosen_option_text: “Or you could just legalize weed everywhere,” suggests your eccentric cousin after gulping down a handful of green gummy bears. “Marijuana isn’t dangerous or anything, so the only thing stopping complete legalization is a bunch of old farts in parliament who are stuck in a more conservative era. Maybe allowing it will let people chill out and not get so mad about this whole federalism thing. Legalizing marijuana might even help the economy because farmers would have a new cash crop to grow. Sounds like a win-win to me!”

title: Particle Accelerator Sparks High Energy Debate
text: Some of The Solutions Guy’s most distinguished physicists have approached you asking for a government grant funding for the Really Big Hadron Collider: the world’s largest - and most expensive - particle accelerator.
chosen_option_text: “Did you know that this experiment has a one in ten million chance of creating a microscopic black hole that will gobble up the whole planet in an apocalyptic chain reaction?” asks Amari Vajiralongkorn, sporting a magnificent tin foil bicorne. “I read it on the internet so it must be true! Scientists may CLAIM it’s safe, but they can’t even design a soda that doesn’t go flat when you shake it! They have NO RIGHT to gamble with our lives. You’ve got to end this mad research at once! If mankind were meant to study atoms, they wouldn’t be so small!”

title: We Won’t, We Won’t Rock You
text: Attendance at last week’s stoning in Risaabussy Square was at a record low, as citizens decided instead to take a healthy walk, read self-improvement books, or merely exchange pleasantries with one another.
chosen_option_text: “If you want these events to draw a crowd, there’s no sense in everyone getting stoned,” chortles rock fan Gyelbu Sisko. “This needs to be a special occasion that lives long in the memories of all those young and old — well, except the victims. We need stadia, lights, loud music and audience participation! Let’s get the crowd rocking!”

title: Honey, We Hung the Parliament
text: The recent national elections in The Solutions Guy saw declining support for the established parties and a big success for the unabashedly populist anarcho-communist party Death to the State. The extremist fringe party, despised by all other parties, gained a surprisingly high number of seats. The government is now in chaos as the more traditional parties scramble to block Death to the State from having any influence on the government.
chosen_option_text: “What utter nonsense!” rebuffs Romulus Golightly, a former Member of Parliament who lost his seat to a suspected arsonist. “The only real solution is holding a new election whenever a stable government can’t be formed. The people of The Solutions Guy are smart; I’m sure they’ll realize what a mistake they made the first time around and restore the order of things. Doing the election over again will be costly, sure, but I really need this gig. I mean, the nation’s ability to be governed is at stake! Yes, that’s the one.”

title: The Great Divide
text: Due to a mix-up at the border, a number of immigrants have been sent backward, downward, upward and sideways to various detention centres across The Solutions Guy. In the midst of the confusion, several thousand children have been separated from their parents.
chosen_option_text: “Seriously?” gasps Ariel Santiago, who just got out of her latest therapy session with her eight-year-old child. “Look at my little Haakon. He was separated from me at the Atharvite border, taken away the moment I asked for asylum. He spent so many months in that state facility that he can hardly talk in Bigtopian, and he keeps trying to arrest the other young children in the playground! You must end this cruel immigration policy immediately. Your country needs more migrant workers, Leader, and my boy needs his mother. A child should never be separated from their parent!”

title: May I Pick Your Brain?
text: A recent exposé has revealed that the wealthy Kennadoof family sent one of their more rebellious daughters to an institution where her brain’s frontal lobe was cut, in a way that destroyed her higher brain functions. She was subsequently hidden from public sight for years. This procedure, called ‘lobotomy’, remains legal in The Solutions Guy. The resulting public backlash has caused quite a headache for your government.
chosen_option_text: “What this ‘activist’ fails to address is that lobotomies can be medically useful,” counters Atticus Dawson, director of the Risaabussy Institute for the Demented, shoving a little boy in front of you. “Just look at little Timmy here: his OCD has been completely cured! Plenty of our patients live better lives after they are cured of their ailments. As such, we need to make sure lobotomies are used for all cases where the unruly and unwell might benefit!”

title: The Woman From AUNT
text: An intelligence team, the “Agents Undercover to Neutralize Troublemakers”, has pinpointed the headquarters of notorious crime boss Sal Bone. Unfortunately, it is concealed within a local orphanage, of which Mr. Bone is a sponsor. Lacking only a smoking gun, AUNT has come to your office with a delicate request.
chosen_option_text: “AUNT would like to launch a mole operation inside the orphanage,” buzzes Special Agent Mia Mozart, radioing in from an undisclosed location. “One problem: none of the team is young enough to pull off an effective inside job. We’ve been kicking around the idea of recruiting and training a few kids — maybe orphans themselves — to act as our eyes and ears. Already got a circus kid named Grayson as a potential candidate. There’s a lot of covert situations where juvenile agents could be useful. If this mission goes well, we could even expand their role into a full-time intelligence division.”

title: Only Leader Can Prevent Forest Fires
text: Large forest fires are raging across The Solutions Guy. Tens of thousands of acres have already been burned, houses in rural communities have been destroyed, and the resultant smoke has drifted into Risaabussy, ruining your plans to spend the day tanning.
chosen_option_text: “All this hand-wringing about forest land management is so interesting,” sarcastically comments Reginald Fils-Aimé, whose family lost their home to the fire. “Oh, wait, no, I don’t care, BECAUSE MY HOUSE BURNT DOWN! Thousands of people have lost their homes and what are you doing about it? We need emergency help now. Let’s take all the money we’re wasting on so-called ‘land management’ and put it into something useful, like disaster relief and rebuilding our homes and communities.”

title: One Small Step for Private Enterprise?
text: Private space companies have expressed a desire to launch a space probe to the moon and other planets in the solar system. To avoid any legal entanglements, they have asked for permission from the government to launch.
chosen_option_text: “You’ve ruined this planet. Now you want to ruin outer space?” queries Gaia Peacedove, an eccentric environmentalist and host of the esoteric television show ‘Antiquated Aliens’, seen dressed in hemp fiber. “Cleanliness is next to godliness, after all. The Ancient Ones didn’t want us to come to them, they will come to us. Stop polluting space with your fancy-schmancy space probes and rockets! Ban all space exploration, and focus on protecting the environment. They will surely see this as a sign that we are ready for their arrival!”

title: State of the Media
text: According to recent surveys conducted by the National Broadcasting Agency, viewership of state media has hit a record low. This has resulted in a wave of officials and state-sponsored journalists seeking your advice on how to improve the situation.
chosen_option_text: “That would be a hideous waste of birthday invites!” objects the State Treasurer, showing you a number of charts that all seem to blend together. “If no one wants to view official media, then they don’t have to. We should scrap the entire thing and let the public come up with their own sources of information and entertainment. The resources could be allocated to somewhere else, like on strengthening our military and funding law enforcement.”

title: Roads Like Roller Coasters, Complain Motorists
text: A group of local motorists have assembled outside of City Hall to protest against the shoddy state of roads in The Solutions Guy.
chosen_option_text: “Why on Earth is it the government’s responsibility to build and maintain roads?” asks bicyclist Faith Hicks, pausing for breath. “Not all citizens own automobiles, you know. The government should be trying to make life better for all, not just car owners! If people want roads, then let private industry build them, and they can charge tolls to the people who actually drive on them. Leave the government out of it!”

title: Power Problems Need Bright Solution
text: The oldest power station in The Solutions Guy suffered a catastrophic failure last night, plunging a third of the power supply grid of Risaabussy into darkness. There is no debate that it needs to be replaced, but the question is with what?
chosen_option_text: “Now the way I see it is that it’s either green, expensive, and sprawling; or compact, polluting and cheap. Wouldn’t it be nice if we had the best of both worlds? Well, we can!” claims fission technician Raphael Cotchin. “Nuclear power is reliable, clean, and although it isn’t cheap, it won’t break the bank. There is a risk of deadly meltdown, but this is relatively small, and the only people who could be against this are anti-nuclear protesters, but what do we care about those tree-hugging hippies?”

title: The Solutions Guy, Bastion of Freedom
text: The Solutions Guy is considered a bastion of personal freedom, granting its citizens many liberties they wouldn’t have in other nations. Most people would consider this a good thing. Politicians are not most people, and now your neighbors are demanding you change your nation’s laws after a spike in the number of tourists and immigrants coming to The Solutions Guy to do things illegal in their homelands.
chosen_option_text: The clicking of a pen draws your attention to the side, “News flash, public relations is where it’s at.” claims the West Calypsan ambassador and propaganda secretary. “When we cracked down on fake news, some subversive journalists hopped the border here to keep publishing unflattering articles about my boss. You leader types have to stick together, I think it’s high time you put reins on the media, end independent news, and make them write more truthful representations about you and us.”

title: Mice in the Walls
text: After a police raid discovered an entire load of smuggled peripheral devices and computer components hidden in the plasterboard walls of an abandoned warehouse, various groups have demanded to repeal the ban of computers.
chosen_option_text: “Pfft, citizens with computers indeed,” says Tracy Kaine, your Minister of Records, while riffling through a cetacean-sized pile of paperwork and ringing phones. “What a preposterous idea. But as The Solutions Guy grows, so do our problems. There is too much data to record, too many records to keep, and too many keeps to earn. We need to allow the government - and only the government - access to computers.”

title: Service With a Snarl
text: The most recent edition of the prestigious Virtual Planet guidebook has praised The Solutions Guy for its many treasures, but also noted how rude wait staff, hoteliers, and tour guides tend to be. Perhaps unwisely, you choose to hold a meeting on the topic in a popular restaurant.
chosen_option_text: “Hate to be like this, but that guidebook has a point,” reluctantly replies the restaurant’s owner after telling off the waiter. “I’ve seen people stand up and leave after being insulted or shouted at by my staff one too many times. It doesn’t matter how many times I replace them - the problem remains. The government should mandate and pay for proper etiquette training for all employees in the service industry, and allow us to fire those who don’t comply. That way the customers are happy and our places of business don’t get bad reviews.”

title: Westfailian Sovereignty
text: After the United Federation sent two police cars, a police helicopter, five drones and a wind-up toy into The Solutions Guy to capture “Mega Momo”, an Atharvite citizen and alleged terrorist, the government has called a special meeting to see what should be done about this blatant breach of sovereignty.
chosen_option_text: “Are you mad?” exclaims Cresta Nagasawa, one of your more queasy ministers, while trying to conceal her worry beads. “The United Federation has Gigadeath 4000 planes, Smashtastic 2000 helicopters and Udienow 500 missiles, and we barely have glorified crop-dusters! We need to engage the international community and try to convince them to join us in enacting sanctions against the United Federation. That will show them we’re serious!”

title: Mayors Behaving Badly
text: Many of The Solutions Guy’s mayors have been getting into hot water in recent months; with allegations ranging from racist commentary to substance abuse, international media are having a field day on highlighting problems in The Solutions Guy’s devolved governments. Concerned citizens are now wondering if higher levels of government should step in and take over city management.
chosen_option_text: “What’s the point of even having the rule of law if our politicians are just going to ignore it?” asks anti-corruption lawyer Michelle Lewis while going through your tax returns. “We need tougher laws and more judges with the gall to enforce them. Even the slightest infraction should result in the immediate dismissal of the mayor. It’ll probably mean more elections, but it’s worth it if it means that the citizenry continue to trust devolved government.”

title: Fancy Some Sparkling Water?
text: A leaked memo has revealed that Sakura, a technologically-advanced neighboring archipelagic country that relies heavily on nuclear power, is planning on releasing several million tons of treated radioactive water previously used to cool their plants out into the open sea. Although Sakura subsequently and rather hastily claimed the treated water is completely harmless, many neighboring countries are not convinced and have asked you to join a conference to decide what should be done.
chosen_option_text: “Why not build a sea wall on our maritime borders?” your Minister for Creative Solutions casually chimes in while shooting crumpled pieces of paper at a trashcan. “Just hear me out. If we build a sea wall we can keep the dirty water out and keep our precious clean water in. The way I see it, it can also keep sea animals and plants safe from pollution of other countries too, right? Well, I guess not but well still be able to keep those pesky foreign ships and fishermen out. Anyway, I think it’s probably time for lunch now. Who’s up for some sushi?”

title: Welfare Programs Not Faring Well
text: A recent lull in legislation has sparked the fires of some bored politicians. After reviewing the back-log of constituent complaints, they’ve come to your desk demanding welfare reform.
chosen_option_text: “Capitalism is the very reason why we need welfare in the first place. Laissez-faire policies would only make the problem worse,” argues political activist Destry Wagner. “If the government took control of all businesses, it could ensure that all employees are paid the amount they need to live - no more, no less - then the problem of providing for the poor would disappear.”

title: Circus Clowns Cause Chaos!
text: Rather than finding them funny, a recent survey shows that most children are actually afraid of clowns. The public is demanding that you do something to stop these terrifying menaces.
chosen_option_text: “Banning clowns is a little extreme, if you ask me,” inputs your Minister for Culture, Billy-Bob Burns. “I think what we need to do is educate children about what clowns actually do. Tell them they aren’t scary and that what they do is actually beneficial! After all, happy kids are less likely to go down the path of crime, which means less spending goes to the police and more funds can be diverted to somewhere important - like my Department!”

title: Drug Deal
text: Preliminary trials of a new immunotherapy drug have suggested that it may achieve remission in bone marrow cancers by up to 28% of formerly untreatable patients. It’s years away from being clinically available, but desperate cancer sufferers are asking for you to expedite this.
chosen_option_text: “Sorry, this is medical science, not faith healing,” snarls unsympathetic-seeming Dr. Earl Annan. “We require multi-phase trials to make sure a medicine is non-toxic, safe in the long term and to make sure it actually really works. It’s a shame that a percentage of the population have to die while we wait, but better to lose a few hundred lives than to compromise scientific integrity. No offence, but these deaths are just unavoidable collateral damage in the war on cancer.”

title: The Path Less Traveled
text: While The Solutions Guy’s northern ports bustle with trade during the summer time, this flurry of activity freezes to a standstill at the onset of winter when thick sheets of ice form over the frigid waters. This seasonal impasse both severely limits economic productivity and makes resupply of the region difficult.
chosen_option_text: “Why don’t we just stockpile before winter?” asks Dallin Pasteur, an advocate of human hibernation. “We bring in everything we need in autumn and don’t worry about nothin’ in winter. You can help defray the cost of our survival by funding winter fuel allowances and cold weather food supplies for the poorest in the area.”

title: Possession, Protection or Poppycock?
text: After tarot cards and a Ouija-board were found in the dormitory of three teenage girls who committed suicide, paranormal objects and occult rites have become the center of a heated debate on the rising popularity of New Age spirituality.
chosen_option_text: “Possession? Are you serious?” queries Lisa Dunn, your unbearably uptight Minister of Conventional Solutions, while closing your curtains so as to not let the sunshine in. “These girls clearly had some issues, but not of the demonic kind. Depressed teenagers need to be dealt with through education and our health system, not through ‘channeling’, dirty bacchanals or waiting for Jupiter to align with Mars. Funky New Age spirituality only makes these things worse, especially for sensitive youngsters. To prevent this kind of thing in the future, we must increase mental health spending and set a minimum age on alternative religion.”

title: A Really Sour Lemon
text: While walking down the street, you notice a lemonade stand consisting of a few cardboard boxes, a pitcher of murky yellow liquid, and a crude rendition of lemons wrought in yellow crayon on paper. Taped to one of the boxes is a prominent notice from the local government, which states that this venture was closed for not meeting standard economic, health, and safety regulations.
chosen_option_text: “Don’t be such a sourpuss; it wouldn’t kill you to buy one of these, y’know,” suggests random bystander Aristotle Garcia, swiping the lemonade out of the kid’s hand. “In fact, I don’t see why children should get special treatment. As long as folks aren’t contradicting the government’s five-year plan, people of all ages should be able to sell products unregulated! And while you’re at it, maybe ease off of some of the other million industrial regulations that are putting us at a disadvantage compared to those vulgar capitalist countries.” He takes a sip from the lemonade, chokes, and stumbles backward into the cardboard boxes with enough force to smash them.

title: Plastic, Plastic Everywhere
text: An unusual alliance of environmental activists and garbagemen have brought to your attention the increasing glut of plastic bags that have been found littering the streets of The Solutions Guy’s cities.
chosen_option_text: “If you can’t get rid of the bags, you must change the bags!” exclaims Ferdinand Montgomery, an environmentalist spokesperson wearing a lab coat and a huge grin. “Scientists have developed plastics that break down over time, so it doesn’t matter where they’re dumped. Require that only biodegradable plastic bags can be sold in The Solutions Guy, and the problem will go away.”

title: Nazi Sympathizers Plan Rally
text: Far-right-wing Nazi supporters plan to stage a rally in the city center tomorrow, giving voice to their violent, racist views.
chosen_option_text: “It’s exactly because we’re civilized that we must let the demonstration proceed,” says free speech campaigner Maria Whitlam. “We may not like what they have to say, but in this society, people have the right to argue whatever political view they want, no matter how hateful, selfish, or stupid it is.”
